dfa182f1cd71430e: PUTRAJAYA: The management swap of National Sports Council (NSC) director-general Jefri Ngadirin and Sports Commissioner Ariffin Ghani is part of the Youth and Sports Ministry's strategy to strengthen the country's sports ecosystem.

Youth and Sports Minister Taufiq Johari said the restructuring took into account the experience and expertise of both officials to enhance the roles of their respective agencies, particularly following the approval of the Sports Development (Amendment) Bill 2026.
Under the transfer, which takes effect on Thursday, Arrifin has been appointed NSC director-general, while Jefri takes over as sports commissioner.

Taufiq said the amendment to the Bill strengthens the powers and role of the sports commissioner, making Jefri's extensive experience dealing with sports associations and athletes an advantage in improving the governance of the country's sports bodies.
"Based on Jefri's experience working with sports associations, athletes and others, we believe his role as Sports Commissioner can be further strengthened.

"Arrifin, meanwhile, has experience as a former athlete, along with other relevant experience that prompted us to carry out this restructuring to make the country's sports ecosystem stronger," he said at a press conference during the Jalur Gemilang handover ceremony for the national contingent to the Dakar Youth Olympic Games in Senegal here on Thursday.

Taufiq explained that the transfers were neither a sudden decision nor one made by an individual, but followed a deliberation process involving the NSC board of directors and the ministry's top management.

"The transfers required a process, although we did not announce it publicly. It was not a decision made by one party or an individual, but one that took various factors into account, including the views of the NSC board of directors and the ministry's management.
"This is part of our strategy to strengthen the country's sports ecosystem ahead of major upcoming events, particularly the 2027 SEA Games, which we will host," he said.
Meanwhile, Arrifin said his appointment as NSC director-general was a major responsibility, describing the new role as an opportunity to return to an organisation where he had previously served.

He said the focus now was to maintain the country's successful momentum at the Commonwealth Games and Asian Games, while ensuring the national contingent could achieve excellent results at next year's SEA Games.
"As the host, we are not just hoping to win, but to win convincingly," he said.

Commenting on preparations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, Arrifin said the NSC would reassess its approach to athlete support programmes, including the Road to Gold (RTG) programme, to ensure promising athletes received the best possible preparation.
He added that he would also examine areas for improvement in the NSC's management, but stressed that these efforts must be undertaken without disrupting the momentum of existing successes.
8d1501395458dfbd: The Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) has reprimanded London's Metropolitan Police Service (MPS) and issued an enforcement notice after officers used a retail crime platform without the force's approval or required data protection checks. Between March 2023 and September 2024, MPS officers registered around 500 free accounts on Auror, a platform retailers use to record crimes such as shoplifting. The force had not formally procured the service or completed the required data protection checks. Retailers such as supermarkets encouraged officers to use Auror and directed them to the platform to access CCTV footage. Auror Europe, registered in England and Wales, is a subsidiary of New Zealand-based Auror. The platform allows retailers to share incident reports, images, and CCTV footage. Retailers pay for access through a browser or mobile app, while police partners use it free of charge. The force had not completed a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) or established data-sharing agreements with Auror Europe, the ICO says. Between August and September 2024, two separate internal security reports were filed regarding officers' use of Auror. The first related to officers uploading the names of suspects they recognized from CCTV footage, and the second pertained to officers collecting CCTV footage from the platform despite no checks being made on it. Access to Auror was blocked as of September 26, 2024. The MPS data protection officer (DPO) informed the ICO of the force's use of Auror in December 2024 during discussion about a separate matter. The watchdog launched a formal probe in April 2025. The ICO found that officers unlawfully uploaded personal data relating to 179 people, including three children, to Auror. For 128, this consisted of names alone; for 49, names and dates of birth; and for two, names, dates of birth, and home addresses. The ICO said the MPS failed to ensure adequate oversight was implemented when deciding what third-party platforms officers were allowed to use – failures that persist today. It claimed the MPS is overly reliant on soft controls to prevent officers from using unapproved software, such as policy reminders and staff training, which often go unnoticed, rather than technical blocks. The ICO also said the force had failed to test whether its web controls worked: officers used Auror for more than 18 months without triggering an alert. The regulator described a repeat failure, pointing to officers' use of Clearview AI in 2021 without proper oversight. The ICO considers the failures ongoing because the force has not demonstrated that its safeguards can prevent similar incidents. The enforcement action compels the MPS to strengthen its safeguards against improper use of third-party tools and provide the ICO with periodic progress updates. David Doodson, head of investigations at the ICO, said: "This action should send a message across the policing sector, and beyond: If you are using new technology to process people's information you must do so lawfully, transparently and with appropriate governance from the outset. "Where organisations fail to protect people's information, we will take action. Our role is not only to hold organisations to account, but to drive improvements and promote the standards people have a right to expect." The MPS told The Register that following the implementation of stricter controls and a pilot scheme, officers in 14 London boroughs are once again using Auror. "Following formal approval and a pilot, the platform is now used in 14 London boroughs," a Met spokesperson said. "It helps officers identify shoplifters more quickly, enabling retailers to directly share evidence and CCTV at the point of reporting and has quadrupled positive outcomes for shoplifting." In an August 2026 announcement, the MPS said the tech, which it did not identify by name, would be rolled out beyond the 14 boroughs and was already deployed in stores such as Tesco, Boots, Greggs, and M&S. It said that instances of shoplifting reported via the platform result in a positive outcome in 29.4 percent of cases. Of the ICO's findings, the spokesperson said: "We accept the ICO's findings that our data protection arrangements at the time were insufficient in relation to individual officers using the Auror platform. "While officers were using the platform in good faith to identify and arrest shoplifters, we recognise that we had not completed the relevant security and data protection work for the platform to be used. "As soon as we became aware of this issue, we immediately suspended access to the platform and carried out a full review. We have subsequently completed the necessary legal, security, commercial and data protection checks before approving the platform for use." This reprimand and enforcement action follow a separate rebuke from the ICO in August, concerning two sensitive cases. In one, a Met officer sent unredacted legal documents to the subject of a stalking protection order, exposing the victim's new home address and contact details. The other saw an officer commit the cardinal CC-not-BCC sin, exposing the email addresses of 18 people linked to Parliament who were targeted in a honeytrap sting. ®
16fc05c2bdd6a1d6: BATU PAHAT: Nearly two weeks after 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal was murdered, her family continues to grieve, missing her laughter and voice.
Her 65-year-old grandfather, Khyar Abas, said he still felt her presence in every corner of their home.
He said the loss was particularly painful as he had been closest to Irene Sofiya, whom he raised following her mother's death eight years ago.
"I really cannot forget my granddaughter. I was always with her, so I feel her loss deeply.
"At times, I feel as though Irene Sofiya is still in every corner of the house, as if she is still here.
"When I see her clothes in her room, I feel emotional. I have not touched her clothes because doing so would make me sad," he said when met at his home in Kampung Parit Selamat, Yong Peng, today.
Khyar said the family home had received a steady stream of visitors since her death, including friends, school representatives and others who knew the teenager.
He thanked those who had visited to offer support and words of encouragement, including well-wishers from outside Johor.
Meanwhile, Irene Sofiya's aunt, Siti Nur Faeza Khyar, 45, expressed hope that the case would be resolved as soon as possible and justice served.
She attended court this morning with two other family members to follow proceedings involving a 16-year-old male student charged with murdering her niece.
She said the family was relieved that the accused had been brought to court and would continue to follow the case until its conclusion.
"We are grateful that he (the accused) has been brought to court. We will continue to follow the developments until the case is concluded," she said.
6bf5f0373b38311f: BRATISLAVA, Oct 15 — Slovakian lawyers Ivan Novotny and Metod Spacek got married in Austria in 2020, but their home country refused to register their marriage—a decision they are now challenging in court.

Novotny, 31, and Spacek, 51, say nationalist Prime Minister Robert Fico’s government is violating an EU court ruling that all bloc members must recognise a same-sex marriage recorded in another member.
They are challenging the Slovakian decision in court in the central European country, where Fico’s government has tightened LGBTQ rights and insists national law takes precedence over EU law.
“We don’t want to feel like second?class citizens,” Novotny told AFP in an interview.
Slovakia has long been one of Europe’s most difficult environments for LGBTQ people.
Public support for equal rights stands at just 35 percent, according to the latest Eurobarometer on Discrimination in the European Union—among the lowest scores in the EU.
In 2022, two men were shot dead by the son of a prominent member of an extreme-right party in front of a Bratislava gay bar.

Fico, who returned to power in 2023, has vowed to build “a barrier against progressivism” and last year changed the constitution to “recognise only two sexes, male and female” in a setback for LGBTQ rights.
Novotny and Spacek said many of their queer friends have already moved abroad.
Politicisation

Novotny and Spacek filed a lawsuit last month against the civil registry after they received a letter signed by Interior Minister Matus Sutaj Estok himself in August, denying their request to register their marriage.
They base their case on last year’s Court of Justice of the European Union ruling that says all EU members must recognise a same-sex marriage recorded in another EU state.
No date for a hearing has been set as yet.
Fico, a four-time premier and supporter of US President Donald Trump, has also personally commented on the case.
“The registration of same-sex marriages is not possible... as it is non-existent under Slovak law,” he said in June.
“We’d look like fools in our own eyes if such a record was achieved,” he added.

Novotny and Spacek—former foreign ministry officials who are both active with different opposition parties—said the refusal to register their union was only issued after a nine-month wait, far surpassing the deadline for such decisions.
“The sheer politicisation of a routine legal act stunned me,” Spacek said.

Other couples are also considering legal action, including seeking redress at the European Court of Human Rights, according to Martin Macko, executive director of LGBTQ rights group Inakost Initiative.
Last month, the Constitutional Court struck down a 2023 petition seeking to extend legal protection to families outside marriage and opening the door to recognising same?sex couples.
In its ruling, however, it recognised that the state has an obligation under European law to establish some form of legal recognition for same-sex couples, Macko said.
Constitutional changes
Fico’s previous government in 2014 had already changed the constitution to define marriage as “a union between man and woman”.
The most recent amendment, passed last year, states that sex cannot be modified and only authorises adoption for married couples, with rare exceptions.
The change also says Slovakia’s “sovereignty” regarding “cultural and ethical questions” should override EU law, leading Brussels to launch legal action against Slovakia last November.
Fico has often clashed with the 27-nation bloc and has faced a series of protests over his policies.
Novotny and Spacek say they will stay in Slovakia for now, despite Fico’s “radical rhetoric”.
But if Fico wins a fifth term in elections due next year, they fear discrimination against LGBTQ people will only worsen and they may leave too, together with their son.
“LGBTQ people would not be safe,” Novotny said. — AFP
f89dff41210a627f: DILI, Oct 15 — East Timor began a three-day school closure today prompted by thick haze that has drifted over from raging forest fires in neighbouring Indonesia.
In the capital Dili, people were out as normal under a yellow-tinged sky, but most were wearing masks, as the government advised a day earlier in announcing the school closures.
Residents welcomed the decision, although they said the pollution had been even worse earlier in the week.
“Recently, the pollution in Dili has been very severe,” 30-year-old midwife Sonya da Costa Soares told AFP.
“We can’t see the sun, the pollution is heavy,” she added.
Though her child is still too young for school, she said the decision to keep students home was “very important so that children are not put in danger.”
Indonesia experiences forest fires regularly during its dry season, but this year the blazes have been especially severe because a strong El Nino has brought drought.

The fires have burned through hundreds of thousands of hectares of forest and plantations in Sumatra, Borneo and Papua, and caused air pollution to surge locally, as well as in Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor.

East Timor’s government said Wednesday it was necessary to close schools “to protect the health of students, teachers and other members of the educational community, given current air quality conditions.”
It urged families to keep children indoors and advised citizens to wear masks if venturing out.
Vitaliano da Costa Calapes, an 18-year-old student at St. Ignatius Loyola College, said he was preparing for upcoming exams.
“We are staying at home, but we are continuing to study... We’re facing our final exams,” he said.
“We believe in the coming days there will be no pollution and school will return to normal, that’s what we hope,” he added.
Felicidade Alves dos Santos Martins, whose daugher Febrianti was home from middle school, said the pollution had been even worse earlier in the week.
“It felt like smoke from fires was covering all of Dili and the mountains,” she said.
“This pollution is very dangerous, it can make us sick.” — AFP
16942863130002b0: KUALA LUMPUR: Imagine buying a house without ever seeing its interior. You have no opportunity to inspect the condition of its floors, walls, bathrooms or kitchen up close.
Yet, you proceed with a bid and successfully acquire the property.
While this may sound daunting to some, buyers who understand the intricacies of property auctions may see it as an attractive opportunity.
The question is whether buying an auction property without viewing its interior is a high-risk move or an opportunity for higher returns.
The answer depends on how well a buyer prepares before placing a bid.
Before bidding, buyers should read the Proclamation of Sale (POS), which is more than just a formality.
The document outlines key details, including the reserve price, deposit, settlement period, buyer's responsibilities and terms of sale.
For first-time auction participants, understanding these details can make the difference between a well-planned purchase and a rushed decision.
One of the main attractions of auction properties is that their reserve prices can sometimes be lower than market prices or those of comparable subsale properties.
For example, a property with an estimated market value of RM400,000 may be offered at a lower reserve price.

This price difference could give buyers an advantage by allowing them to acquire a property below its market value. However, the gap between the reserve price and market value should not automatically be regarded as a profit.

More importantly, buyers must calculate the total cost of acquiring the property. This includes the purchase price, legal fees, stamp duty, financing costs, registration fees and any repair or renovation expenses.
If the property remains attractively priced relative to its market value after accounting for these costs, that is where its real potential lies.
Many people still assume that auction properties are necessarily damaged, burdened by substantial arrears or occupied by people who are difficult to evict.
In reality, not all auction properties fall into these categories. They can range from apartments, condominiums and serviced apartments to terraced houses and commercial properties.
The condition and risks vary from one property to another. Therefore, auction properties should not automatically be regarded as high-risk investments.
Instead, each property should be assessed based on its condition and the information available.
One of the main reasons buyers are hesitant to purchase auction properties is that they may not be allowed to enter and inspect the interior before bidding.
While it is true that auction buyers may not have the same opportunity to conduct internal inspections as subsale buyers, this does not mean they have to bid blindly.
Available property information, photographs, location, external condition, building management details and information contained in the POS can help buyers make an initial assessment.

Buyers can also seek information from relevant parties and consult a lawyer before making a decision. In other words, buying an auction property is not simply a matter of being brave or cautious but of knowing what to check.
Another common concern is what happens if the property is still occupied.
Some auction properties may indeed be occupied by former owners, tenants or squatters.
This must be taken into account, as ownership of a property does not necessarily mean the buyer can immediately move in and take possession on the same day.

However, this does not automatically make the property an unworthy purchase. What matters is that buyers understand the property's status, the terms of the POS and the procedures required after the purchase.
Any action to remove occupants must also be carried out through the proper legal channels.
Outstanding land tax, assessment tax, maintenance charges and other fees are additional concerns that often deter buyers from auction properties.
Again, these are not matters to be feared blindly but costs that must be calculated.
Buyers should establish what arrears exist, who is responsible for them and how these liabilities are addressed in the POS.

They should not focus solely on the reserve price while overlooking other potential costs. In some cases, even after accounting for additional expenses, the overall cost of the property may remain attractive compared with other options on the market.

This is where the potential for higher returns begins. Buyers who are willing to conduct the necessary checks and calculate costs carefully may have an opportunity to acquire properties at more attractive prices.
For some buyers, the price difference could provide room for renovations, rental income or potential capital appreciation in the future, depending on the property's location and market conditions.
Auction properties do carry certain risks, but risk does not necessarily mean a purchase is not worthwhile.
In fact, risks that are identified and properly assessed can form part of a strategy to achieve higher returns.
Consider two buyers looking at the same property. The first focuses only on the price and becomes apprehensive upon hearing about arrears, occupants or the property's condition.
The second conducts due diligence, calculates all costs, assesses the location, secures financing and understands the POS.
The second buyer is not necessarily taking on greater risk. Instead, they are better prepared to manage it.
This is what distinguishes buying an auction property by chance from making a strategic investment.

For investors, auction properties can also offer opportunities to acquire assets at attractive prices, upgrade them and potentially benefit from capital appreciation or rental income, depending on the location and market conditions.
For first-time homebuyers, auction properties may also be worth considering, provided the price, financing arrangements and purchase are within their financial means.
Therefore, buyers should not dismiss auction properties simply because of the risks involved. As with any property purchase, knowledge and preparation are essential.
Instead of asking only, "How cheap is this property?", buyers should also ask, "How much will I actually have to spend, and what value will I get in return?"
In the auction property market, a low price may open the door to an opportunity, while risks must be understood and managed.

For those who understand the process, conduct the necessary checks and know the intricacies of property auctions, auction properties are more than just an alternative option. They could potentially be a gold mine.
The writer is a lawyer at Tetuan Nazri Azmi Islinda.

3744d602892ed765: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is almost certain to forge an alliance with other political parties ahead of the Melaka state election, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said today, although he stopped short of revealing who its potential partners might be.
According to Utusan Malaysia, Takiyuddin put the likelihood of cooperation at nearly 100 per cent when questioned about the Opposition coalition’s preparations for the upcoming polls.
“It’s around 100 per cent. Not more than 100 per cent,” he told a press conference in Parliament.
His remarks come just two days after Barisan Nasional (BN) suggested it was close to securing an electoral partner, with negotiations said to have reached 90 per cent mutual understanding.
However, BN has insisted that any potential ally must be trustworthy and would not “stab it in the back”.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki declined to identify the parties involved in the discussions but hinted at the kind of political partners BN would be willing to work with.
Takiyuddin did not disclose which parties PN was negotiating with or whether the talks involved BN.
He said discussions over seat allocations were already under way, both with potential allies and among PN’s own component parties.
“Discussions have been ongoing for some time between us and the parties cooperating with us, as well as among our own component parties.
“We are discussing seat allocations and the necessary thorough preparations that we need to make,” he said.
The uncertainty over PN’s electoral arrangements comes as the coalition faces a separate legal obstacle that could prevent it from contesting under its own name and logo.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS) suspended all PN activities with effect from September 23, leaving the coalition unable to use its name and symbol while the order remains in force.
Asked how PN intended to contest the election if the suspension was not lifted, Takiyuddin said alternative arrangements were already being considered but declined to elaborate.

“There is an alternative for everything. The first option, of course, is the Perikatan Nasional logo. If that cannot be used, there are other alternatives, but these are strategies that cannot be disclosed.
“Otherwise, it wouldn’t be a strategy. If we announce it, it becomes a tragedy,” he quipped.
The Melaka state election is scheduled for November 14, with nominations on October 31 and early voting on November 10, following the dissolution of the state assembly on September 23.
In the previous election in 2021, BN secured a commanding majority with 21 of the 28 seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won five and PN two.
The coalition’s legal difficulties follow notices issued by the RoS on September 22 concerning its registration and activities.
On Tuesday, the Kuala Lumpur High Court granted PN permission to challenge the RoS action through a judicial review but refused its application for an immediate stay of the suspension order.
Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad ruled that PN could proceed with its legal challenge but declined to temporarily lift the suspension pending further proceedings.
The court has fixed October 22 to hear PN’s application for a stay of the order, with both sides given an opportunity to present their arguments.
Until then, PN remains barred from using its name and logo, while its activities remain suspended, complicating its preparations for the Melaka election.
49dd076ec955fe91: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Zetrix AI Bhd will fully cooperate with authorities in an ongoing joint investigation by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, the company said its operations remained unaffected by the investigation.

The company was responding to a query from Bursa Malaysia Securities dated Oct 14 regarding a media report entitled "Police say six witnesses questioned in probe into MyEG, Zetrix AI” published by The Edge Malaysia on Oct 13.
Zetrix AI said it would communicate any material developments through official announcements.
The company said it would make necessary announcements on material developments as appropriate. — Bernama
bb7e56c737dba765: AS the new school year gets under way in Austria, a headscarf ban for girls under 14 has sparked protests on the streets and in the classroom, with dozens of pupils refusing to comply.
Austria's conservative-led government has insisted that the ban, introduced on Sept 1, promotes gender equality and protects Muslim girls from "segregation and oppression."
But critics argue that it disproportionately targets Muslims, infringes upon religious freedom and is forcing young girls to dress in a way that makes them feel uncomfortable.
Since the ban took effect, education authorities across Austria have held 127 meetings with parents and filed 52 reports over alleged breaches of the law, according to the education ministry.
Opponents of the ban have also held protests across the country, with several hundred people gathering each time.
At a demonstration in Vienna, Zehra, 37, who did not want to give her last name, said her two daughters, aged nine and 13, were "sad and angry" about the ban.
"We raise our children by telling them, you can decide who you want to be – and this law is the exact opposite," she said.
Seham, 12, said she felt "afraid" to remove her headscarf at school "because I'd worn it for two years and it felt like a part of me."
After discussions with school leaders, she said she was allowed to cover her hair with an alternative non-traditional head covering, but would still "rather wear the full headscarf."
Roughly eight per cent of Austria's nine million residents are Muslim, according to 2021 government statistics.
They suffer the highest rates of racism and discrimination against Muslims in the EU, according to a 2024 report by Europe's FRA rights agency.
In the 2024 elections, the far-right Freedom Party won for the first time even though it failed to form a government. The anti-immigration party continues to top voter opinion polls.
The new law is Austria's second attempt to restrict headscarves in schools after a coalition between the conservatives and the Freedom Party introduced a ban for primary school pupils in 2019.
That law was overturned by the constitutional court on the grounds that a regulation targeting only Muslims was incompatible with religious neutrality.

The Islamic Religious Community in Austria, which is supporting legal action against the new headscarf ban, said it had received around 70 reports from families about difficulties during its implementation.
"A law that was justified as protecting children's welfare is putting precisely those children under pressure at school," the group said in a statement.
The constitutional court confirmed to AFP that it had received a legal complaint about the law and a decision is expected in the first half of 2027.
When girls refuse to comply with the law, schools are required to hold a series of discussions with pupils and their parents before cases are referred to education authorities.
Ultimately, parents who continue to ignore the ban can be fined.
In a statement sent to AFP, Education Minister Christoph Wiederkehr said the fact there had only been 127 meetings so far showed "that the vast majority of pupils and parents are cooperative."
"In addition, the figures show that the discussions held with the parents concerned in the event of a violation are, for the most part, successful," he added.
Education authorities in Vienna said that "on the basis of the discussions held so far, the impression has emerged that the girls wish to wear the headscarf of their own accord."
Sandy, 12, said she began wearing a headscarf about a year ago because "I place a lot of importance on my religion and I want to be able to live it."
A teacher who has worked with two affected girls in the capital told AFP there was no sign they were being forced to wear headscarves.
The girls had spent weeks adapting to the new rules and searching for acceptable alternatives to headscarves, said the teacher, who wished to remain anonymous.
"It is very uncomfortable for them."
* The writers are from AFP

4866715f5782996a: SHAH ALAM, Oct 15 — A former director of an education centre at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to two charges of abusing his position to secure employment contracts worth RM3.12 million in 2022.
Datuk Prof Muhammad Hussin, 64, a retiree, entered the plea after the charges were read out before Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin.

According to the charges, Muhammad, a member of Koperasi Siswazah Bangi Berhad (KSBB), allegedly abused his position to secure two contracts worth RM1.2 million and RM1.92 million respectively to manage the Master of Education programme through UKM’s Faculty of Education.

He was accused of influencing KSBB board members at two separate meetings to approve the appointment of QTech Management Malaysia Sdn Bhd, a company in which he purportedly had an interest, as the programme operator.
The alleged offences took place on Feb 26 and June 25, 2022, at Kolej Keris Mas, UKM, and Hotel Tenera in Bangi, respectively.

Muhammad was charged under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 (Act 694), which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the value of the gratification involved, if it can be valued or is monetary in nature, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.

MACC deputy public prosecutor Muaz Ahmad Khairuddin proposed bail of RM300,000, with additional conditions requiring the accused to report to the MACC office, surrender his passport to the court and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses.

Defence counsel Muhammad Wafi Anwar Roslan sought a lower bail of RM50,000, citing his client’s financial circumstances, including his responsibility for two wives and nine children, and his reliance on a monthly pension as his sole source of income.

“The accused also suffers from synovial sarcoma and heart disease, both of which require regular treatment. I also urge the court not to impose the passport surrender condition, as his second wife and child are in Indonesia,” he said.
The court set bail at RM80,000 and ordered the accused to surrender his passport and refrain from interfering with prosecution witnesses.
The case was fixed for mention on Nov 12. — Bernama
7d936ee4a6ddf1fe: KUALA LUMPUR: The BA of Malaysia (BAM) is facing difficulties finding a quality replacement for national mixed doubles head coach Nova Widianto, who left on July 31.

BAM performance committee chairman Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei said efforts to recruit an experienced coach had been limited as most preferred candidates remained under contract with their respective teams until the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

He said BAM had contacted several candidates, including former national coach Chin Eei Hui, who is now based in New Zealand, and Jeremy Gan, who is working in Hong Kong, but both remain tied to contracts.
"We are still looking. It is not easy to find a coach because most of them are already under contract until the 2028 Olympics.
"We have offered the position to several local coaches, but they all still have contracts. We understand their situation and need to find another solution," Chong Wei said.

Chong Wei said BAM needed to find a solution soon, as next year would be an important period for Malaysian badminton, particularly with the start of the qualifying process for the 2028 Olympics approaching.
He said if a suitable candidate could not be identified, BAM would have to consider alternative measures to ensure the national mixed doubles team's preparations were not affected.
Commenting on reports linking national junior doubles head coach Pang Cheh Chang to the position, Chong Wei confirmed that his name was on the shortlist, but no final decision had been made.

"His name is indeed on the shortlist, but we have not made a decision. We need to discuss the matter at committee level to determine our first, second and third choices before submitting the names to BAM president Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz for approval.
"Only after receiving approval can we announce the decision," he added.
Nova left BAM to rejoin Indonesia's national team after helping Chen Tang Jie-Toh Ee Wei win the mixed doubles world title in Paris last year.
5650173a630a9eae: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are still awaiting the full report from the Chemistry Department and pathology findings to determine the cause of a man's death in custody on Oct 1.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the detainee, a local man in his 40s, died at 1.52am while receiving treatment at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM).
"The detainee was taken to hospital after he was reported to be unwell but died while receiving treatment.
"The cause of death has yet to be determined, and we are still waiting for the full report from the Chemistry Department.
"We hope everyone will be patient and wait for the official pathology findings," he said at a press conference today.

He said the case had been classified as sudden death (SDR), while the investigation was being handled by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Unit for Deaths in Custody, with the cooperation of the Integrity and Standards Compliance Department.
He said the investigation was also examining all evidence to determine whether there had been any misconduct or breach of standard operating procedures (SOPs) in handling the detainee.
Asked whether detention procedures had been followed in the case, Fadil confirmed that they had.
However, he said the Bukit Aman investigation was ongoing to establish the cause of death and examine the possibility of misconduct or SOP violations.
He said the man had a record of 44 criminal offences, including 18 drug-related cases.
He said the man was arrested following three police reports against him, involving one drug-related case and two criminal cases.
"In the drug case, investigated under Section 39A(1) and Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, the deputy public prosecutor decided on Sept 22 that no further action would be taken.
"This decision was made after investigations found that the man had no control over or possession of the seized drugs.
"In the second case, investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code, police obtained positive fingerprint evidence at the scene," he said.
However, Fadil said the deputy public prosecutor had directed on Oct 1 that the man be charged under Section 448 of the Penal Code.

2cbc520f9c82553a: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's data centre ambitions are gathering pace, with 84 projects approved nationwide as of July, including 27 flagship developments carrying an estimated investment value of RM225.97 billion and the potential to create 4,053 jobs.

But as billions of ringgit pour into the sector, the challenge is no longer just attracting investors. It is ensuring the projects deliver lasting economic benefits without placing excessive pressure on the country's electricity, water and infrastructure resources.
Between 2021 and mid-2025, MIDA approved RM144.4 billion in data centre and cloud computing investments.

Olive Tree Property Consultants chief executive officer Samuel Tan said the rapid expansion marked a significant shift in Malaysia's economic development, with construction activity accelerating across Johor, Selangor and Negri Sembilan.

"It is an economic shift decades in the making and, with construction gathering pace across three key states, Malaysia's digital future is no longer a vision. It is being built, powered and staffed by Malaysians today," he told NST Property.
The 27 flagship developments are being fast-tracked under the Data Centre Task Force (DCTF), with Johor accounting for 16 approved projects, followed by Selangor with 10 and Negri Sembilan with one.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said one facility was already operational, while the remaining projects were under construction.
To ensure local businesses benefit from the investment wave, the government has imposed a minimum local content requirement of 30 per cent for every DCTF-approved project.
However, the scale of investment has intensified debate over whether the economic returns justify the substantial resources required to build and operate these facilities.
MALAYSIA MUST REFINE ITS DATA CENTRE STRATEGY

Zerin Properties said concerns raised in a recent commentary, "Data Centre Missteps?", published in a recent English daily, about Malaysia's aggressive pursuit of data centre foreign direct investment (FDI), reflected the challenges of managing a rapidly expanding industry.

The commentary questioned the government's approach, citing pressure on resources, limited direct job creation and the Finance Ministry's push to reprice data centre investments as evidence of a flawed policy.

While these concerns warranted attention, Zerin Properties' founder and chief executive officer, Previndran Singhe, said Malaysia's economic history showed that the country had repeatedly entered new resource and industrial growth cycles before refining policies to capture greater domestic value.

Malaysia's development has been shaped by successive industries, from tin and rubber to palm oil, oil and gas, and manufacturing. The electrical and electronics sector subsequently deepened the country's integration into global supply chains.
"In every case, the early phase was lopsided: capital intensive, foreign controlled, and concentrated in a narrow set of benefits, before we recalibrated and captured more value downstream.

"Data centres are simply the latest version of that same story. It is a capital-intensive, resource-intensive industry that arrived in Malaysia because of genuine structural advantages, faster than our policy settings were calibrated to manage it.
"The answer to that mismatch was never to walk away from the industry. It is the same tool Malaysia has reached for every time before: recalibrate the terms as the market matures," Previndran said.
MALAYSIA'S GEOGRAPHICAL ADVANTAGES REMAIN SIGNIFICANT
Previndran said Malaysia's appeal to data centre investors rested on structural advantages, including land availability, access to electricity and water, and proximity to Singapore.

Singapore's constraints on land and power capacity for new large-scale facilities have created opportunities for Malaysia to accommodate additional digital infrastructure while remaining close to the city-state's financial and technology ecosystem.

"Our geography puts us within the low latency radius that matters for data centre siting relative to Singapore's finance and technology demand, at a time when Singapore has largely run out of land and power headroom for new large-scale facilities.
"A capacity constrained neighbour with deep demand, sitting next to a country with the land and energy base to build at scale, is a structural and durable advantage. It is not temporary arbitrage."
Previndran said the reported RM145 billion in committed data centre investments should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of a policy mistake.
Instead, the commitments demonstrated that investors recognised Malaysia's competitive position, even as policymakers worked to ensure the country received an appropriate return.
He said the challenge was one of timing, with investments arriving before pricing mechanisms, infrastructure safeguards and policies to capture more domestic value were fully developed.
Concerns over electricity tariffs, water security, lending concentration and relatively low direct employment during the operational phase remained legitimate, he said.

Data centres require substantial electricity and cooling resources but typically employ fewer permanent workers than many traditional manufacturing facilities. Rapid development can also strain local infrastructure if capacity fails to keep pace.
These challenges called for stronger approval conditions rather than a wholesale retreat from the industry, Previndren said.

Data centres in Johor, Selangor and Negeri Sembilan consumed about 28.68 million litres of water daily as of January 2026, with projected demand linked to developments in the three states expected to reach 445.04 million litres a day between 2025 and 2030.
FOUR PRIORITIES TO MAXIMISE ECONOMIC BENEFITS
Previndran outlined several measures to ensure future data centre investments deliver stronger economic and social returns.
First, investment incentives must evolve with market conditions.
Tax concessions and preferential utility arrangements should be reviewed as resource costs, infrastructure constraints and project contributions change.
New approvals should reflect prevailing electricity and water availability rather than assumptions made when the investment pipeline was first established.

Where existing agreements permit renegotiation, adjustments should be transparent and commercially credible. Future projects should also have clear review mechanisms from the outset, providing greater certainty for investors while protecting the public interest.
Previndren said the Finance Ministry's push to reprice data centre investments highlighted the need for a systematic approach rather than ad hoc adjustments.
Second, new capacity must support the energy transition.
Malaysia should accelerate the development of grid-connected renewable energy and strengthen its electricity infrastructure to accommodate rising demand.
Previndran also called for serious evaluation of next-generation energy options, including small modular nuclear reactors, as they become commercially viable.

"Malaysia should be accelerating grid-connected renewables and seriously evaluating next-generation baseload options, including small modular reactors as they become commercially viable, instead of leaning on conventional capacity expansion alone.

"Tying new data centre approvals to renewable procurement commitments, as some competing jurisdictions already require, pushes the incentive structure toward genuinely additive green capacity rather than simply reallocating what already exists," he said.
Third, water efficiency should become a baseline requirement.

Cooling technologies differ significantly in their water and energy requirements. Immersion cooling and other liquid-cooling systems can improve efficiency in suitable applications, while well-designed closed-loop systems can reduce water consumption.
However, Previndran said no single technology was appropriate for every facility, and lower-water cooling systems must also be assessed for their electricity use and overall environmental impact.
"Mandating the best available cooling technology for new approvals, rather than grandfathering older, thirstier designs, should be a baseline requirement, not an aspiration," he said.
Fourth, planning and environmental safeguards must keep pace.
Previndran said complaints about noise, water pressure and disruption to nearby communities highlighted the need for better planning and enforcement.

Minimum separation distances from residential areas, environmental impact assessments where required, enforceable operating conditions and meaningful community consultation should form part of a more rigorous approval framework.
Site selection must also take into account the capacity of electricity networks, water infrastructure, roads and other essential services, he said.
Turning investment commitments into national gains
Previndran said the RM145 billion in committed investments represented a significant opportunity, but the headline figure alone did not establish the ultimate economic benefit to Malaysia.
The priority was to ensure that investments translated into productive domestic activity, skilled employment, local procurement, technology transfer and sustainable economic gains.

"It is leverage we have not yet fully used. Malaysia entered this cycle, as it has entered every prior resource cycle, ahead of its own regulatory readiness. The mistake would be to conclude from that timing gap that the industry itself was miscalculated.

"The more useful conclusion, and the one the Finance Ministry's own "repricing" comment quietly reaches, is that our incentive and planning framework needs to catch up to the market, gate by gate, the same way it has after every cycle we have capitalised on before.

"The opportunity is real, and so are the challenges that come with it. The task is not to retreat but to adapt. Malaysia's challenge has never been attracting opportunity. Our challenge has always been learning how to capture a greater share of the value it creates. Data centres are simply the latest chapter in that story," Previndran said.

367f073b98508a43: BANGKOK, Oct 15 — The International Monetary Fund expects energy-rich Middle Eastern economies to bounce back, but not in the medium term, the organisation’s regional chief said today, as fighting continued between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis.

“We will not go back to the pre-war trajectory in the medium term because this shock will have a scarring impact on various sectors and also will disrupt a certain number of infrastructure, and will require additional spending in order to increase resilience,” IMF regional director Jihad Azour told reporters.

37d3ca05128918b5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — When a Sarawak clinic manager opened his banking app and discovered a mysterious 10-digit balance, he did what some people might do when faced with an eye-watering number: he asked ChatGPT.
The answer? A whopping RM1 billion.
But for Wan Muhammad Fairus, 33, whose account should have contained less than RM1,000, his unexpected brush with billionaire status was over almost as quickly as it began.
According to Berita Harian, the father of four from Samariang, Kuching, was in his bedroom preparing to make a banking transaction when he stumbled upon the extraordinary balance.

“I was in my bedroom at the time, about to make a transaction. If I’m not mistaken, I had less than RM1,000 in my account. When I opened the app and tapped the icon to reveal my balance, I was shocked to see such an enormous amount of money.
“I was completely stunned! My hands were shaking as I held my phone. I tried logging out and logging back in, but the money was still there.
“It was only after checking my bank statement and asking ChatGPT how much the figure amounted to that I realised it was RM1 billion,” he said with a laugh when contacted by the newspaper.
The bizarre discovery soon caught the attention of social media users after Wan Muhammad Fairus shared a screenshot of his online banking app showing the astonishing 10-digit figure.
But rather than start planning how to spend his newfound fortune, he suspected something was amiss.
Knowing the money was not his, he contacted the bank to find out what had gone wrong.
He said he never considered touching the windfall, aware that spending money mistakenly credited to his account could land him in legal trouble.
“After I contacted the bank, they informed me that there had been a technical problem and temporarily froze my account until 4pm yesterday.
“Everything was resolved after the bank reversed the transaction, and the money originally in my account was unaffected,” he said.
And while his billionaire moment may have been short-lived, there could still be a little something in it for him.
Wan Muhammad Fairus said the bank had mentioned the possibility of a reward, although he had yet to receive anything or find out what it might be.

“The bank also mentioned that they wanted to give me a reward, but I haven’t received anything yet and don’t know what it will be. Perhaps I’ll have to wait for an email notification or an announcement from them,” he said.
For now, his account is back to normal — and his extraordinary billion-ringgit surprise has become a story to tell.

ffff458d968dc99d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — The Street Fighter movie opens today in Malaysia — will it do better than its other 80s franchise counterpart Masters of the Universe (which I did enjoy)?
I grew up with two younger brothers who loved the arcade.
That meant watching over them as they would mash buttons playing Street Fighter, though the male friends I hung out with were also big fighting game fans.

Ryu, Ken, Chun Li — even if you didn’t play the games they were such recognisable characters to most kids who grew up in the 80s (though my ex would argue that Tekken is the superior fighting game franchise).
There are movies that pay homage to the 80s; Street Fighter sets the whole film in the era, going for a less polished, grittier look and CRT TV vibe.
It’s high camp all around, with scenes played for laughs and dialogue that has more cheese than a Kraft warehouse.
If you’ve played the games, you might appreciate the effort put into ensuring that the characters’ signature moves are used in the movie, instead of just generic fight choreography.
There is a fair amount of animation used in the film that will remind you of the age when we’d spend either 5.30pm or Saturday mornings watching cartoons.
Perhaps Capcom/Legendary Pictures decided animating sequences instead of doing full flashback scenes was both thematically and financially suitable.
Production decisions aside, how did Street Fighter hold up as a movie?
If you’re expecting deep characterisation and a compelling script, this isn’t it.

What it is — a movie for those wishing they could go back to the days of 80s childhood, when everything was hyper-optimistic, all things seemed possible, all rendered in bright colours and embracing all things that youngsters now would find “cringe.”

For newer, younger audiences, a lot of the references would probably go over their heads and with some grisly deaths, blood and of course, heavy beat-em-up sessions, maybe don’t bring the under-10s to the movie.
There’s also a fair bit of sexual innuendo in the jokes but they’re the kind that always existed in kid shows, meant for only adults to understand or kids, decades later upon rewatching.
As for the cast, I think they did a good job — working well as an ensemble without any one single actor standing out above the rest.
Though I do have to give Noah Centineo his props as Ken, perhaps the one character that gets a full emotional arc in the film.
Also to all the people complaining that Callina Liang as Chun Li didn’t show enough skin, this is Street Fighter not Flesh Displayer.

Liang’s dialogue throughout the movie is generally terrible but she deserves kudos for being able to say it all with a straight face while displaying the athleticism required of a character often described as the “strongest woman in the world.”
I did not expect to like Jason Momoa’s performance as much as I did; am not spoiling who he’s playing but he brings a fitting physicality to the role and perfect comedic timing.
Is Street Fighter worth spending two hours of your day for?

If you need a film that will cerebrally take you out of the present moment, letting you forget that outside there’s a Middle East conflict, a shouting orange is leading the biggest Western superpower and everything looks like a Silent Hill game outside, there are far worse things to do with your time.
Colourful, full of nostalgia bait and embracing the silliest parts of Street Fighter, the film knows exactly who it’s made for.

c7010c71aee8374d: VIENNA, Oct 15 — As the new school year gets under way in Austria, a headscarf ban for girls under 14 has sparked protests on the streets and in the classroom, with dozens of pupils refusing to comply.
Austria’s conservative-led government has insisted that the ban, introduced on September 1, promotes gender equality and protects Muslim girls from “segregation and oppression”.
But critics argue that it disproportionately targets Muslims, infringes upon religious freedom and is forcing young girls to dress in a way that makes them feel uncomfortable.
Since the ban took effect, education authorities across Austria have held 127 meetings with parents and filed 52 reports over alleged breaches of the law, according to the education ministry.
Opponents of the ban have also held protests across the country, with several hundred people gathering each time.
Part of me
At a demonstration in Vienna, Zehra, 37, who did not want to give her last name, said her two daughters, aged nine and 13, were “sad and angry” about the ban.
“We raise our children by telling them, you can decide who you want to be—and this law is the exact opposite,” she said.
Seham, 12, said she felt “afraid” to remove her headscarf at school “because I’d worn it for two years and it felt like a part of me”.
After discussions with school leaders, she said she was allowed to cover her hair with an alternative non-traditional head covering, but would still “rather wear the full headscarf”.
Roughly eight percent of Austria’s nine million residents are Muslim, according to 2021 government statistics.
They suffer the highest rates of racism and discrimination against Muslims in the EU, according to a 2024 report by Europe’s FRA rights agency.
In the 2024 elections, the far-right Freedom Party won for the first time even though it failed to form a government. The anti-immigration party continues to top voter opinion polls.
The new law is Austria’s second attempt to restrict headscarves in schools after a coalition between the conservatives and the Freedom Party introduced a ban for primary school pupils in 2019.
That law was overturned by the constitutional court on the grounds that a regulation targeting only Muslims was incompatible with religious neutrality.
Under pressure

The Islamic Religious Community in Austria, which is supporting legal action against the new headscarf ban, said it had received around 70 reports from families about difficulties during its implementation.
“A law that was justified as protecting children’s welfare is putting precisely those children under pressure at school,” the group said in a statement.
The constitutional court confirmed to AFP that it had received a legal complaint about the law and a decision is expected in the first half of 2027.
When girls refuse to comply with the law, schools are required to hold a series of discussions with pupils and their parents before cases are referred to education authorities.
Ultimately, parents who continue to ignore the ban can be fined.
In a statement sent to AFP, Education Minister Christoph Wiederkehr said the fact there had only been 127 meetings so far showed “that the vast majority of pupils and parents are cooperative”.
“In addition, the figures show that the discussions held with the parents concerned in the event of a violation are, for the most part, successful,” he added.
Education authorities in Vienna said that “on the basis of the discussions held so far, the impression has emerged that the girls wish to wear the headscarf of their own accord”.
Sandy, 12, said she began wearing a headscarf about a year ago because “I place a lot of importance on my religion and I want to be able to live it”.
A teacher who has worked with two affected girls in the capital told AFP there was no sign they were being forced to wear headscarves.

The girls had spent weeks adapting to the new rules and searching for acceptable alternatives to headscarves, said the teacher, who wished to remain anonymous. “It is very uncomfortable for them.” — AFP
58a928225508e54d: SYDNEY, Oct 15 — Australia’s navy said today it would audit bathrooms across its fleet after a video recording device was found in the cabin of one of its ships.
Navy chief Matt Buckley has vowed a full investigation into the incident aboard the HMAS Leeuwin, a survey ship docked in the northeastern city of Cairns in the state of Queensland.
A member of the armed forces has been identified as a “person of interest” and was assisting military police with enquiries, Australia’s defence ministry said in an update today.
Buckley called the act a “most despicable betrayal of trust” and said authorities are “undertaking a 100 percent audit of all of our bathrooms across the Fleet”.
“My highest priority, as always, is the wellbeing of our people. All potentially impacted personnel are receiving our strongest support,” the vice admiral said in a statement.
“You have my assurance and commitment that we will tackle this act of sexual violence with all of our energy. Any perpetrator will be held to account.”

The defence ministry said late Wednesday that the issue was under investigation, after a lawmaker said she had received a message from a former member of the navy claiming concealed cameras had been found in the women’s showers.

“Even more disturbing are claims that footage from these cameras may have been uploaded online before the cameras were discovered,” said Senator Jacqui Lambie, a prominent advocate for the armed forces.
“How many of our female sailors have unknowingly been recorded in their most private moments? How much footage has been distributed online so far, retained or uploaded without knowledge or consent?”
A royal commission that concluded in 2024 found that sexual misconduct remained a “systemic issue” across the Australian armed forces. — AFP

11173ab0d16bae9a: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 15 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng has urged Malaysia to consider legal action against Indonesia to seek compensation for the worsening transboundary haze crisis if Jakarta refuses to cooperate with a proposed permanent Asean firefighting task force.

Lim said the recurring crisis, which has forced schools to close and disrupted livelihoods, could no longer be treated as an annual inconvenience, calling for a coordinated regional response to tackle forest and land fires at their source.

In his speech during the Budget 2027 debate in the Dewan Rakyat today, the former finance minister proposed establishing a permanent Asean task force involving Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and the Philippines, with rescue personnel available throughout the year to respond swiftly to outbreaks of forest and land fires.

The call comes as Malaysia continues to grapple with deteriorating air quality caused by smoke from forest and land fires in Indonesia, with 34 of the country’s 68 air monitoring stations recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today.

Klang and Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest readings at 192, approaching the very unhealthy threshold of 201. The haze has also disrupted daily life, with schools in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and several states ordered to close on October 9 to protect students from exposure to polluted air.

“If the Indonesian government continues to reject the Asean task force on grounds of national sovereignty, the Malaysian government will have no choice but to initiate legal action to seek compensation,” he said, according to the text of his speech.
“Malaysians can no longer remain silent and take no action in the face of this recurring haze crisis.”
The DAP national adviser said forest and land fires in Indonesia had affected an estimated 300,000 hectares this year, an area more than 70 per cent larger than that recorded in 2025.
He also criticised Jakarta for what he described as its reluctance to accept foreign assistance, including offers from Malaysia, despite the growing scale of the fires.

“It is deeply regrettable that the Indonesian government has refused to continue accepting international assistance from Japan, which has already ended, or to promptly accept offers of assistance from foreign countries, including Malaysia,” he said.
“Its justification is that Indonesia is capable of handling the forest and land fires, although the reality suggests otherwise.”

Lim argued that a permanent regional response team, rather than temporary arrangements activated only during emergencies, would allow ASEAN countries to tackle fires before the resulting smoke spread across national borders.

He also called on the Malaysian government to provide financial assistance to people whose incomes have been affected by the haze, particularly gig economy workers and Grab drivers who rely on outdoor work.
“Our schools have been closed, while workers, particularly those in the gig economy and Grab drivers, have been forced to stop working because of the haze crisis,” he said.
“The long-term health effects have yet to be determined. In short, the government should provide financial assistance to those affected.”
Lim said the haze was threatening not only public health and children’s safety but also Malaysia’s economic prosperity, making a lasting regional solution increasingly urgent.
His proposals formed part of a wider speech in support of Budget 2027, which was tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on October 9.
The haze has become a growing regional concern, with fires in Indonesia affecting air quality across neighbouring countries, including Malaysia and Singapore.

On October 11, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia was still awaiting Indonesia’s response to its offer to send a firefighting aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help tackle the blazes, according to Bernama.
Indonesia, meanwhile, said on October 13 that it would assess foreign offers of assistance based on their effectiveness in supporting firefighting operations, according to CNA.
fa613fbbcd4b4a9d: KUALA LUMPUR: A clinic manager was left stunned when his online banking account appeared to show a balance of RM1 billion, despite having less than RM1,000 in it moments earlier.
The unusual incident went viral after Wan Muhammad Fairus, 33, shared a screenshot showing the 10-digit figure on his banking app, along with his account of the experience.
The father of four, who lives in Kuching, Sarawak said he was in his bedroom preparing to make a transaction when he noticed the unusually large balance.

"At the time, I was in my bedroom about to make a transaction. If I remember correctly, my account balance was below RM1,000. When I opened the app and tapped the icon to hide the balance, I was shocked to see such a huge amount.
"I was really shocked! My hands were shaking as I held my phone. I tried logging out and logging in again, but the money was still there.
"Only after checking my bank statement and asking ChatGPT what the figure meant did I realise it amounted to RM1 billion," he said when contacted.
Realising that the money was not his, Wan Muhammad Fairus suspected a technical error and immediately contacted the bank for clarification.
He said he had no intention of using the money, knowing it did not belong to him and fearing possible legal consequences.
"After I contacted the bank, they informed me that there had been a technical issue and temporarily blocked my account until 4pm yesterday.
"Everything was resolved after the bank reversed the transaction, and the original amount in my account was unaffected.

"The bank did mention that it wanted to give me a reward, but I have not received anything yet and do not know what it will be. Perhaps I have to wait for an email or an announcement from them," he said.
ac212b6a4fad4b05: LONDON, Oct 15 — British comedian and actor Russell Brand was described by prosecutors as “ruthless” and a “sexual predator” as they outlined allegations of rape and sexual assault involving six women at a London court yesterday.
According to BBC News, the 51-year-old faces three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault over alleged incidents between 1999 and 2009, all of which he denies.
Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC told Southwark Crown Court that the six complainants did not know one another and had come forward independently.
She alleged that Brand used his charm and humour to pursue sexual encounters, describing his desire for sexual contact as “indiscriminate and voracious”.
The jury heard allegations involving women whom Brand encountered at a Labour Party conference in 1999, during his work in the entertainment industry and at performances in London.

Among the allegations were claims that he raped a woman after meeting her at the political conference, sexually assaulted women at media workplaces and raped another woman following an initially consensual encounter in 2009.
Prosecutors said one complainant subsequently confronted Brand by text message over his treatment of her, to which he allegedly apologised.
Brand has maintained that he never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, with prosecutors telling the court that he had disputed the allegations when questioned by police.
The court also heard testimony from Brand’s former flatmate Mark Pinheiro, who said the comedian had told him he might have gone a “bit too far” with a woman during the 1999 Labour Party conference.
Pinheiro maintained under cross-examination that he remembered Brand making the remark, although he was questioned about the accuracy of his recollection.
Brand, who attended court accompanied by his wife Laura, became famous through television and radio before appearing in Hollywood films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall and Get Him to the Greek.
The trial continues and is expected to last six weeks.
ac2995f2a7ca7d54: KUALA LUMPUR: National track cycling star Azizulhasni Awang failed to reach the keirin semi-finals of the World Championships after finishing last in quarter-final Heat 3 at the Shanghai Velodrome on Thursday.
