43df790fc02940f7: PETALING JAYA: Sarawak DAP chief and Padungan assemblyman Chong Chieng Jen was suspended from the Sarawak state assembly for the remainder of the current session after a motion alleging that he misled the assembly about Sarawak’s 2027 budget document and acted improperly during its debate was passed today.

Dayak Daily reported that the motion was moved by state transport minister and Senadin assemblyman Lee Kim Shin and seconded by minister in the premier’s department and Kakus assemblyman John Sikie Tayai.
Sixty-two assemblymen voted in favour and one against while another abstained.
The motion alleged that Chong deliberately misled the Dewan on Oct 13 and acted improperly during the budget debate on Oct 14, including by repeatedly making allegations he could not substantiate.
It accused him of using offensive and insulting language against fellow assemblymen and imputing improper motives to them.
In tabling the motion, Lee referred to Chong’s remarks on Oct 13, when Chong questioned the reliability of the budget document after highlighting a pagination issue.
Lee quoted Chong as saying: "And more importantly, if such a serious error can be made in basic document pagination, what confidence do we have in the budget document’s more detailed figures?"
Lee then referred to the speaker’s response on Oct 14, when Asfia Awang Nassar described Chong’s remark as "uncalled for and mischievous".

"Under Standing Order 32(12), any member who makes any statement in the Dewan that deliberately misleads the Dewan is deemed to be out of order or to be in contempt," Asfia was quoted as saying in the Hansard.
Lee also highlighted Chong’s remarks to the speaker: "So, Tuan Speaker, you have wasted a lot of my time… I know you are in control, but please be fair to me…"
Another remark cited in the motion was Chong’s statement about Kota Sentosa assemblyman Wilfred Yap: "Kota Sentosa is hallucinating. He thought something criminal was being committed."
Lee said the Standing Orders provided a framework for vigorous debate while preserving the dignity and orderly proceedings of the Dewan.

"All members of this House have the right to speak, question, disagree and scrutinise the government. These are essential features of parliamentary democracy and must be respected. Those rights, however, carry responsibilities.
"Every member must observe the Standing Orders, respect the authority of the chair, and exercise care in making statements and allegations in the House," he said.
7705a267993532f8: WASHINGTON: The US military has developed strike plans that could include using the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast Bomb, also known as the "mother of all bombs", against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites if president Donald Trump orders renewed combat operations, CNN reported on Thursday citing US officials familiar with the matter.

The potential deployment of the largest non-nuclear bomb in the US arsenal would mark a significant escalation in the conflict, although officials familiar with military planning discussions told CNN questions remain over its effectiveness in achieving Washington's strategic objectives.
Reuters could not immediately verify the report.
feb25b31ddca56f1: MUMBAI: India's Jio Platforms, the digital arm of conglomerate Reliance Industries, is aiming to raise more than US$3 billion in what would be the country's biggest-ever initial public offering, after announcing pricing details ahead of next week's launch.
The company, controlled by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, is looking to sell 270 million new shares at 1,065-1,119 rupees (US$11.22-US$11.79) each, it said in a statement late Wednesday.
A sale at the top end of the range would raise around US$3.2 billion, surpassing the previous national IPO record of US$2.9 billion set by Hyundai Motor India in 2024.
The IPO opens for subscriptions on Oct 21, with a view to listing a week later.

Reliance Industries, India's most valuable listed company, has been pushing to expand beyond its traditional oil refining and petrochemicals businesses into telecoms, digital services and green energy, with Jio Platforms at the heart of that strategy.

While Jio has expanded into areas ranging from artificial intelligence to enterprise network services, it is best known for telecoms subsidiary Jio Infocomm, India's largest mobile operator by subscribers.
Launched a decade ago, Jio's wireless service disrupted the market with steep discounts that helped it rapidly win customers from rivals Bharti Airtel and Vodafone.
The carrier now has more than 530 million subscribers and handles roughly 60% of India's mobile data traffic.

The company raised more than US$20 billion in 2020 from global investors and technology giants including Meta and Alphabet, funding an ambitious digital ecosystem spanning payments, entertainment streaming and online services.
e1df467615d55c8e: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan sedang mempertimbangkan cadangan menyita aset pesalah trafik yang disabitkan dengan kesalahan serius bagi membayar pampasan kepada mangsa kemalangan jalan raya dan keluarga mereka, kata Menteri Pengangkutan Loke Siew Fook.
Beliau berkata langkah itu antara beberapa pilihan yang sedang diteliti bagi memastikan mangsa atau keluarga mereka tetap menerima pampasan, khususnya apabila pesalah tidak mampu membuat bayaran.
"Kami juga sedang meneliti sama ada aset pesalah boleh disita," katanya di Dewan Rakyat.
Loke berkata kerajaan turut mengkaji kemungkinan mengenakan denda lebih berat atau hukuman penjara terhadap pesalah yang gagal membayar pampasan, seperti yang diperuntukkan dalam undang-undang lain.
Bagaimanapun, beliau menjelaskan kerajaan belum membuat sebarang keputusan mengenai kaedah pelaksanaan sistem pampasan yang dicadangkan itu.

Beliau menjawab soalan Ahmad Saad (PN-Pokok Sena) yang ingin mengetahui bagaimana keluarga mangsa boleh mendapatkan pampasan sekiranya pesalah tidak mampu membayarnya, terutama bagi menampung kehilangan pendapatan dan perbelanjaan sara hidup selepas kemalangan.

Loke berkata, Jemaah Menteri pada 15 Julai lalu bersetuju secara prinsip untuk meminda Akta Pengangkutan Jalan 1987 bagi membolehkan mahkamah memerintahkan pesalah trafik yang disabitkan dengan kesalahan serius membayar pampasan kepada mangsa atau keluarga mereka.

Pampasan itu akan dikenakan sebagai tambahan kepada hukuman sedia ada seperti penjara, denda dan larangan memandu, membabitkan kesalahan yang menyebabkan kematian, kecederaan parah atau hilang upaya kekal.

Menurutnya, Kementerian Pengangkutan sedang bekerjasama dengan agensi kerajaan lain bagi memperincikan cadangan berkenaan, dengan pindaan undang-undang itu dijangka dibentangkan di Parlimen pada awal 2027.
Ahmad turut bertanya sama ada kerajaan akan mempertimbangkan pelaksanaan konsep 'diyat' dalam Islam, iaitu pembayaran pampasan kewangan kepada mangsa atau keluarga mereka.

Menjawab perkara itu, Loke berkata kementeriannya terbuka menerima pandangan pakar perundangan Islam, namun menegaskan undang-undang yang dicadangkan akan terpakai kepada semua pihak tanpa mengira agama.
Sementara itu, menjawab soalan Syahredzan Johan (PH-Bangi), Loke berkata pindaan berkenaan turut merangkumi penambahbaikan sistem mata demerit kesalahan trafik.
Beliau menyifatkan sistem sedia ada kurang berkesan kerana mata demerit hanya direkodkan selepas pesalah membayar saman, sekali gus melemahkan fungsinya untuk mencegah pemanduan berbahaya.
5d768ec10799ff9d: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has tightened conditions for data centres, with operators now required to pay the market electricity tariff rate and the full cost of their reserved power capacity, even if they use less.

Investment, trade and industry minister Johari Ghani said electricity tariffs for data centres had been separated from those imposed on other consumers to ensure that the sector no longer benefits from subsidies meant for households and other industries.
"Previously, if investors requested 200 megawatts (MW), we would provide it, but they might only use 100MW (and pay for that amount).
"Now, even if they use only 100MW, they must still pay for the full 200MW," he told the Dewan Rakyat in reply to a question from Rodziah Ismail (PH-Ampang).

Johari said investors would also be required to bear the cost of upgrading Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) electricity transmission network and adopt water recycling technology to reduce pressure on state water supplies.
He said the Data Centre Task Force also required investors to source at least 3% of their services locally, including consultancy, contracting, engineering and legal services.
This requirement is aimed at ensuring that local businesses benefit from the growing number of data centre investments, he added.
"We want to tell the world that we welcome their investments, but it is no longer about cheap energy. The country and its people must benefit from these investments."
Johari said data centres' contribution to the economy rose sharply from RM900 million in 2021 to RM14.1 billion this year.

There are 57 data centres currently operating in Malaysia, with a combined electricity supply of 6,237MW from TNB, while another 60 projects requiring 11,172MW are at various stages of approval and construction.
Johari said total reported investments in the sector had reached RM385.7 billion, with RM271 billion coming from foreign investors and RM114 billion from domestic investors.

Major technology companies such as Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google and Alibaba are also being encouraged to provide local universities and businesses with access to computing resources, and to share artificial intelligence and cloud computing technologies.
Johari said these efforts were crucial to developing local expertise and building a skilled workforce over the long term.
def304bf6487298a: LONDON: Celine Dion has joined the Barbie universe, with a new doll inspired by one of the most recognisable moments of her career.
The Barbie Signature doll recreates the navy, long-sleeved dress Dion wore when she performed “My Heart Will Go On”, the theme song from “Titanic”, at the 1998 Academy Awards.
Its hair is swept into an updo and paired with silver earrings, while a blue necklace provides an unmistakable nod to the fictional “Heart of the Ocean” jewel at the centre of the 1997 blockbuster.
“It is a true honour to join the Barbie legacy with a doll inspired by one of the most meaningful moments of my career,” Dion said.
“I hope this doll inspires everyone to express themselves with confidence, follow their dreams, and believe in the power of their own voice.”

The Canadian singer joins a growing list of music stars to receive the Barbie treatment, including Mariah Carey and Tina Turner. Margot Robbie, who starred in the 2023 “Barbie” film, has also been immortalised in doll form.

Dion has sold nearly 260 million albums worldwide, with hits including “Because You Loved Me” and the enduring “My Heart Will Go On”. The latter became inseparable from “Titanic” after its release, winning the Academy Award for best original song and becoming one of Dion’s signature recordings.

The new doll also arrives after a difficult few years for the singer. Dion revealed in 2022 that she had been diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome, a rare neurological disorder, and subsequently stepped away from performing.
She returned to the stage last month for a series of shows near Paris, marking another chapter in a stellar career spanning more than four decades.
b82adcdf6b929255: PETALING JAYA: Private daycare and kindergarten operators expect fees to rise by up to 20% when the new RM2,000 minimum wage kicks in next June and increases operating costs.

Malaysian Association of Kindergartens (PTM) chairman Elvis Gan said rising labour costs, along with higher costs for food, hygiene items and learning materials, would strain operators’ finances and prompt fee revisions.
He said operators’ ability to absorb higher wage costs would depend on the number of children enrolled, fee collections and other operating commitments.
Private daycare fees are currently estimated at RM700 to RM1,000 a month, while private kindergarten fees range from RM500 to RM1,500 a month, depending on location, amenities and service packages.

"For example, a RM300 wage increase for one caregiver equals an added cost of RM100 per baby at a ratio of three babies to one babysitter, RM60 per child at a ratio of 1:5, or RM30 at a ratio of 1:10.

"However, this calculation assumes the stated ratios and excludes employer contributions and other employment costs. It also does not represent the fee increase rate proposed by PTM," Gan said, according to Utusan Malaysia.

Association of Registered Child Care Providers Malaysia (ARCPM) president Norsheila Abdullah said private daycare centres, especially smaller operators, risked shutting down without adequate support to cope with higher costs.
She said the closure of daycare centres would not only cause caregivers to lose their jobs but also limit parents’ access to safe and accessible childcare services.
"Children may be placed at facilities that lack proper training, monitoring or safety standards. These risks need to be prevented through policy before problems occur," she said.
Gan said PTM proposed targeted wage subsidies for eligible registered kindergarten operators, especially during the adjustment period, to help offset higher labour costs.
He said grants for training and safety equipment, along with assistance to secure affordable premises, could help reduce expenses for daycare and kindergarten operators.

"We propose fee assistance for families in need, including parents who cannot benefit from tax relief. Bulk purchases of essential goods and group training with the association can also save costs without affecting caregiver adequacy, nutrition, education quality and children’s safety," he said.
Meanwhile, ARCPM proposed studies on the impact of higher costs on private daycare centres, especially those serving low-income families or operating in areas with few childcare facilities.

Norsheila also proposed dedicated funding for childcare and early childhood development, separate from funding for formal education, saying quality childcare should begin before children enter kindergarten or school.
e51e82753ab26e14: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 15 — Malaysia recorded a 4.5 per cent decline in live births in 2025, while the total fertility rate (TFR) fell to 1.5 children per woman, reflecting a continued downward trend in the country's birth rate.
According to the Vital Statistics, Malaysia, 2026 report released by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) today, 396,175 live births were recorded last year, down 18,743 from 414,918 in 2024.
The crude birth rate (CBR) also recorded a decrease from 12.2 births in 2024 to 11.6 births per 1,000 population in 2025.

“CBR for all major ethnic groups recorded a decrease in 2025 as compared to 2024. Malays recorded the highest CBR with 14.9 births, while Chinese remained to record the lowest CBR with 5.0 births per 1,000 population in 2025,” DOSM said in a statement.
All states recorded lower birth rates in 2025, with Terengganu recording the highest CBR with 18.7 births and Penang recording the lowest at 9.3 births per 1,000 population.
According to the report, the country's TFR fell from 1.6 children per woman in 2024 to 1.5 in 2025.

Malays remained unchanged and continued to record the highest TFR with 1.9 children per woman aged 15-49 years. The TFR for Indians remained unchanged at 1.1 children, while Chinese recorded the lowest TFR, declining from 0.9 children to 0.7 children in 2025.

At the state level, Terengganu recorded the highest TFR with 2.5 children in 2025, followed by Kelantan (2.3) and Pahang (1.8). In contrast, Penang recorded the lowest TFR with 1.1 children, declining from 1.2 children in 2024.

The number of deaths increased by 0.4 per cent (815 deaths) from 198,992 deaths in 2024 to 199,807 deaths in 2025. The crude death rate (CDR) remained unchanged at 5.8 deaths per 1,000 population in 2025.
Indians recorded the highest CDR at 8.2 deaths, while Other Bumiputera recorded the lowest CDR at 5.7 deaths in 2025. The CDR for Chinese decreased from 7.6 (2024) to 7.5 (2025).
At the state level, Perak recorded the highest CDR with 8.2 deaths, while Putrajaya recorded the lowest CDR with 2.6 deaths per 1,000 population. — Bernama
fed075c42841b341: BOGOTA: Thousands of Colombians took to the streets of cities across the country on Wednesday to protest the policies of new right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella.
The demonstrations mark the first show of force by the opposition since de la Espriella took office in August vowing to combat crime and eradicate "narco-terrorists."
Trade unionists, Indigenous Colombians, students and feminists gathered at a rally in Bogota led by former left-wing president Gustavo Petro.
"It's going to fall!" demonstrators chanted, referring to Colombia's most right-wing government in decades.
What began as peaceful protests during the day grew heated in some areas as night fell, with riot police deployments, water cannons and tear gas.

Opposition senator Maria Eugenia Londono said on X that "heavy repressive deployments" had been reported in various spots around the country, from downtown Bogota to Popayan, Cauca and Ibague, Tolima.
Bogota Councilor Ana Teresa Bernal posted on X that riot police "attacked" groups of young people and musicians with "stun grenades and water cannon".
No guarantees
Petro headed Colombia's first-ever leftist administration, which expanded free access to public universities, oversaw record increases to the minimum wage and improved labor conditions for employees.
Leftists fear that these advances are under threat from his successor, a US-backed millionaire who is part of a US-backed right-wing wave sweeping Latin America.
"I feel like we have no guarantees and that the little we did obtain...we're about to lose," teacher Ester Guerra, 32, told AFP in Bogota.
De la Espriella is one of the most divisive Colombian leaders of modern times.
He has been cheered by conservatives for taking the fight to guerrilla groups that refused to lay down arms a decade ago when the powerful FARC rebel army disbanded.
His critics accuse him of endangering the country's fragile peace process, threatening minority rights and of showing an authoritarian streak.
"Everything we have fought for for so long is at risk today," said Unzo Vargas, a 44-year-old civil servant, who protested in Bogota with a rainbow flag for the LGBTQ community.
Fear and constitutional rights
On the eve of the marches, de la Espriella issued a decree giving authorities greater powers to crack down on demonstrations in the event of damage to property or blocking of streets.
"Violence, vandalism and blockades that trample on the rights of millions of citizens will not be tolerated," he wrote on X.
The president's threat to unleash force on demonstrators was slammed by his opponents as an attempt to silence critics.
"They're trying to frighten the population so people don't go out to protest, but it's a constitutional right," said Oscar Perez, a 40-year-old teacher.
Protesters also voiced strong disapproval of de la Espriella's foreign policy.

A trained lawyer, he has restored diplomatic relations with Israel, which Petro broke off over the country's offensive in Gaza, and announced controversial plans to recognize Jerusalem as Israel's capital.
De la Espriella is also an enthusiastic US ally, and protesters burned an American flag in the streets of the capital while others waved Palestinian flags.
"Yankees go home," read a placard held aloft by a demonstrator in Colombia's second city of Medellin.
Left-wing Senator Ivan Cepeda, who lost a June election runoff to de la Espriella by less than a percentage point, also attended the march in Bogota.
b17059c6f8a9469a: PETALING JAYA: Jabatan Penjara sedang meneliti dakwaan berhubung masalah kekurangan bekalan air dan tahap kebersihan yang tidak memuaskan di Penjara Kajang, serta memberi jaminan tindakan segera akan diambil sekiranya terdapat sebarang kelemahan.
Jabatan itu berkata penelitian dibuat susulan dakwaan Lawyers for Liberty (LFL) mengenai gangguan bekalan air, kemudahan sanitasi dan penyediaan makanan di penjara berkenaan.
"Kami sedang meneliti dakwaan tersebut bagi mengenal pasti keadaan sebenar dan memastikan setiap isu yang dibangkitkan diberi perhatian sewajarnya," menurut kenyataan.
"Penambahbaikan segera akan diberi keutamaan bagi menangani sebarang kelemahan yang dikenal pasti, khususnya membabitkan kemudahan asas, kebersihan dan kebajikan banduan."
LFL mendakwa Penjara Kajang yang menempatkan 5,000 banduan berdepan masalah kekurangan air serius sehingga menyukarkan mereka mandi dan menggunakan tandas.
Menurut kumpulan itu, aliran air terlalu perlahan sehingga banduan terpaksa mengambil masa berjam-jam untuk memenuhi sebaldi air, malah ada yang tidak dapat menggunakan tandas sehingga dua hari.
LFL turut mendakwa setiap bilik hanya dibekalkan satu liter air minuman sehari, selain membangkitkan kebimbangan mengenai dulang makanan yang kotor dan tahap kebersihan makanan yang tidak memuaskan.

Sehubungan itu, LFL menggesa kerajaan dan pihak berkuasa penjara segera menangani masalah berkenaan serta memastikan banduan mendapat bekalan air bersih yang mencukupi dan kemudahan sanitasi yang sempurna.

Sementara itu, Jabatan Penjara menegaskan pihaknya sentiasa mengutamakan kebajikan, kesihatan, kebersihan dan keselamatan banduan, termasuk memastikan keperluan asas disediakan mengikut peraturan serta prosedur ditetapkan.

Jabatan itu turut menasihatkan orang ramai supaya merujuk saluran rasminya bagi mendapatkan maklumat yang tepat dan disahkan, selain tidak membuat spekulasi atau menyebarkan maklumat yang belum dipastikan kesahihannya.
4a1cce9e3a536f4a: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is considering seizing the assets of motorists convicted of serious traffic offences to pay compensation to road accident victims and their families, transport minister Loke Siew Fook said today.
He said the proposal was among the measures being studied to ensure that families receive compensation, particularly when offenders cannot afford to pay.
"We are also looking at whether offenders’ assets can be seized," he told the Dewan Rakyat.
Loke said the government was also looking at whether offenders who failed to pay compensation could face heavier fines or jail terms, as provided for under other laws.
However, he said no decision had been made on how the proposed compensation system would work.

He was responding to Ahmad Saad (PN-Pokok Sena), who asked how families would receive compensation if offenders could not pay, especially in light of lost income and living expenses following an accident.
Loke said the Cabinet agreed in principle on July 15 to amend the Road Transport Act 1987 to allow courts to order motorists convicted of serious offences to compensate victims or their families.
The proposed compensation would be on top of existing punishments such as jail, fines and driving bans, and would cover offences involving deaths, serious injuries or permanent disabilities.
Loke said the transport ministry was working with other government agencies to finalise the details, with plans to table the amendments in Parliament in early 2027.
Ahmad also asked whether the government would consider the Islamic principle of "diyat" or financial compensation to victims or their families.

aaa6fd554e0db3b0: PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia recorded a 4.5% decline in live births in 2025 while the total fertility rate (TFR) fell to 1.5 children per woman, reflecting a continued downward trend in the country's birth rate.
According to the statistics department, 396,175 live births were recorded last year, down 18,743 from 414,918 in 2024.
The crude birth rate (CBR) also decreased from 12.2 births in 2024 to 11.6 births per 1,000 population in 2025.

"The CBR for all major ethnic groups decreased in 2025 compared with 2024. The Malays recorded the highest CBR with 14.9 births, while the Chinese continued to record the lowest CBR with five births per 1,000 population in 2025," the department said in a statement.
All states recorded lower birth rates in 2025, with Terengganu recording the highest CBR at 18.7 births and Penang recording the lowest at 9.3 births per 1,000 population.
According to the report, the country's TFR fell from 1.6 children per woman in 2024 to 1.5 in 2025.

The Malays continued to record the highest TFR with 1.9 children per woman aged 15-49 years. The rate for Indians remained unchanged at 1.1 children, while the Chinese recorded the lowest rate, declining from 0.9 children to 0.7 children in 2025.

At the state level, Terengganu recorded the highest TFR at 2.5 children in 2025, followed by Kelantan (2.3) and Pahang (1.8). In contrast, Penang recorded the lowest TFR at 1.1 children, declining from 1.2 children in 2024.
The number of deaths increased by 0.4% (815 deaths) from 198,992 deaths in 2024 to 199,807 deaths in 2025. The crude death rate (CDR) remained unchanged at 5.8 deaths per 1,000 population in 2025.
Indians recorded the highest CDR at 8.2 deaths while other Bumiputeras recorded the lowest CDR at 5.7 deaths in 2025. The CDR for the Chinese decreased from 7.6 in 2024 to 7.5 last year.
At the state level, Perak recorded the highest CDR at 8.2 deaths, while Putrajaya recorded the lowest CDR at 2.6 deaths per 1,000 population.

bdb5f9d6d0998937: As artificial intelligence use becomes more widespread, scholars are working to understand its effects on the people who use it. MIT Professor Eric So offers one of the most complete syntheses yet, in his new book, “The Collision: What AI Does to Us,” published this month by W.W. Norton. Recognizing that AI offers opportunities to complete work faster, and in some cases has been turned into useful domain-specific tools, So nonetheless looks at the costs of relying on it too broadly. He contends that heavy use of AI can lead to a kind of cognitive atrophy, in which people fail to develop and retain essential thinking skills. In general, he says, evidence shows that our ability to learn gets dramatically better when we wrestle with material, work through initial failures, keep iterating, and in the process acquire better thinking skills while retaining more knowledge.  These conclusions are drawn from recent research by So and others, in academia and industry, including analysis from AI firms themselves, such as an Anthropic study showing that about half of queries from college students were low-effort queries for simple answers. So also weaves personal reflections into his narrative — having long studied financial markets and behavior, he is familiar with analyzing how new tools and information affect our decisions. MIT News talked to So, who is the Sloan Distinguished Professor of Global Economics and Behavioral Science in the MIT Sloan School of Management, about the book.  Q: What prompted you to write “The Collision”?    A: I wrote this book in response to patterns I was seeing in myself and other individuals. I open the book with this story where I was instinctively reaching for AI to help me think through problems I normally would have handled myself. A colleague had reached out for assistance and I had essentially taken her question and written half a sentence, then said, “ChatGPT, help me finish this professionally.” I made a few light edits and sent it off. And I sat back and really felt incredibly concerned about how I had removed my own thinking from the process. I have found students are outsourcing their thinking to AI, rather than thinking through things themselves, turning to it to answer homework that would normally help them build mastery in a subject. We need to start understanding what this technology is doing to us and how it interacts with human cognition and our psychology, and give people some practical insights.  Q: Part of that means understanding the incentives people have to use AI, or how the allure of AI takes hold, even when there are long-term costs, in your view.  A: There are converging factors drawing us to AI. For example we have a real biological instinct to conserve our mental energy, and socially, we face situations where AI is used by other people to race ahead, and it rachets up the pressure on everyone else to use AI. Combine that with the problems detecting AI use in a practical way, and all these factors create what I call “AI gravity,” this constant pull to use AI. It’s not simply a matter of telling people to think for themselves. At this moment we’re in, AI is colliding with society. Q: So we need to look at these systemic factors, not just individual decisions, when it comes to AI use, like businesses urging employees to use it.  A: Many organizations are not just suggesting use of AI: It is now the basis of your evaluation, meaning if you want a bonus or promotion, it is incumbent upon you to use these tools. I think a subtle process is taking hold in academia, where people say, “My future employer will want me to use AI, so I’d better start using it now.” But the problem is that as you start to use AI now, we’re losing touch with the practices and capabilities we’re seeking to build, and in turn that makes us more dependent on using AI in the future, and it becomes a self-fulfilling prophecy. Q: What is AI doing to our minds?  A: AI is not just changing what we can do, it’s changing who we are as thinkers. AI removes a lot of the friction necessary to build foundational mastery. It is causing many people to lose their capacity for pushing through problems. AI offers instant relief, and we become accustomed to that. Many people are turning to it as an access point for information, so it’s affecting our ability to remember. Also, AI is changing our interpersonal relationships. A key point in the book is that these models are simultaneously sycophantic, meaning they want to make us happy because that’s how they drive engagement and get positive feedback, but they are also really persuasive. We lose the ability to connect with other people because we’re so accustomed to this frictionless environment where the models always agree with us. Q: Your book emphasizes the value of “productive struggle.” You write, “Struggle doesn’t mean you’re suffering.” Instead, we get a handle on things by struggling to learn them.  A: We need to recast how we think about struggle, as something that is formative rather than a problem to be solved. I draw a lot of parallels in the book between some of the societal changes that occurred post-industrialization, when suddenly people no longer needed to be physically active to be economically productive. We saw more people suddenly develop physical exercise as something we do intentionally, that required reframing of what physical struggle meant. And I think we need that sort of shift about what we think about cognitive struggle.  Q: Given all this, what can we do to maintain some reasonable level of cognitive effort today? A: At the personal level, I emphasize four principles for navigating this age of AI. One is embracing the struggle, as we’ve talked about. The second rule is: Value who you are without AI. I’ve seen so many presentations over the last couple of years where someone has put together this very polished-looking presentation with Claude, but when they present it, it’s clear they didn’t put in the work necessary to understand the material. The formative struggle creates what I refer to as an “inseparable task bundle,” since making the slides allows me to engage in substantive discussion. In the absence of valuing who you are without AI, we get the product, but not the ability to capitalize on it. The third rule is about reinvesting your cognitive surplus. There are a lot of tasks for which AI can save you time — rote activities — but it matters what you do with those time savings. If you’re just funneling the same energy into the same tasks, you’re missing out on the potential transformational benefits of AI. The most innovative changes are not the ones that simply allow us to automate, but stretch the capabilities of  humanity in a productive way and build expertise. Or, people can channel that freed-up time to focus on family, learn a new language, cultivate skills.  The last rule is about using AI as your cognitive trainer. AI is this dual force, where it is very bad for thinking if you use it as an answer machine, but can be great for learning if you use it as a tutor. AI can be tailored to you. However, it requires that you seek out the friction of having a tutor, relative to having an answer machine. And that requires motivation.  This is a very challenging moment, and the problem is one we need to take seriously.

943c6910da212752: Di Malaysia, apa sahaja bisa menjadi isu politik. Termasuklah bahasa, sebagaimana tindakan sesetengah netizen cuba mengapi dan mengasapkan pemulauan terhadap rantaian kedai kopi (kopitiam) Oriental Kopi dengan alasan pelayannya kurang mahir berbahasa Melayu, selain menunya tidak cermat kerana tiada di dalam bahasa kebangsaan.
Selamat datang ke politik berbahasa di Malaysia. Apakah dimensi politik bahasa ini? Bagaimanakah cultural authority sedia ada bermain peranan?

Ketika menyampaikan titah diraja pada Istiadat Pembukaan Penggal Kelima Majlis Parlimen ke-15 di Parlimen pada 19 Jan 2026, Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim bertitah sebarang usaha untuk mengadakan sistem pendidikan baharu mesti dibuat selari dengan dasar pendidikan kebangsaan. Satu hal yang menonjol pada ucapan baginda itu adalah penegasan agar bahasa Melayu menjadi bahasa utama kerana ia adalah bahasa kebangsaan. "Oleh itu, sebarang usul untuk mengiktiraf apa juga sistem pendidikan lain mesti menerima bahasa Melayu dan sejarah Malaysia".

Isu ini bukanlah sederhana, ia membawa kita kembali kepada persoalan kewarganegaraan di mana bukan Melayu yang bersedia menerima identiti Malaysia perlu menerima pula bahasa Melayu sebagai bahasa rasmi, mestilah boleh dan bersedia bertutur dalam bahasa tersebut. Titah Sultan Ibrahim tersebut tidak syak lagi merupakan singgungan mengenai isu berkait UEC (Sijil Peperiksaan Bersepadu).

UEC adalah peperiksaan berpusat yang dikendalikan oleh Sekolah Menengah Persendirian Cina (SMPC) di bawah Gabungan Persatuan Guru Sekolah Cina Malaysia (Jiao Zong). Ia bukanlah peperiksaan di bawah Kementerian Pendidikan dan tiada kaitan dengan Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina di bawah Kementerian Pendidikan. Kelemahan atau ketidakmampuan sebahagian besar pelajar berbangsa Cina menguasai bahasa Melayu bukanlah sesuatu yang terbina dari persepsi politik tetapi telah pun dibuktikan dalam pelbagai kajian akademik, antara lain oleh Ang Lay Hoon dan Che Radiah Mezah, menerusi makalah ilmiah 'Masalah Penggunaan Bahasa Melayu dalam Kalangan Pelajar Etnik Cina di Malaysia' pada tahun 2012.

Masyarakat Cina berusaha melobi parti-parti politik untuk mengiktiraf UEC. Mereka yang menyokong pengiktirafan UEC menegaskan ia adalah bahagian daripada hak asasi manusia, akses adil kepada pendidikan dan peluang kerjaya, dan sama sekali bukan satu ancaman kepada bahasa kebangsaan, iaitu bahasa Melayu. Isu ini ditunggang oleh ahli-ahli parti politik khusus dalam helah memomokkan kelompok masyarakat Cina yang dianggap gagal mengasimilasi kebudayaan kebangsaan. Manakala, kelompok kanan Melayu pula beranggapan ia sebagai satu ancaman dan sengaja mencabar Dasar Pendidikan Kebangsaan, di mana naratif yang diketengahkan adalah UEC tidak selari dengan Falsafah Pendidikan Kebangsaan memandangkan silibus sejarah dan bahasa pengantar di sekolah persendirian Cina ini menggunakan bahasa Mandarin.

Loke Siew Fook, setiausaha agung DAP, parti yang mendapat sokongan meluas pengundi berbangsa Cina berulang kali menyatakan bahawa sebahagian besar pelajar UEC menguasai bahasa Melayu dan mengambil peperiksaan Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) bagi memastikan kelayakan mereka menepati standard kebangsaan.

Untuk mengambil jalan tengah, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menyatakan kerajaan tidak mengiktiraf sukatan pelajaran UEC secara rasmi, sebaliknya sekadar memberikan laluan bersyarat untuk kemasukan lulusan tertentu ke institusi pendidikan tinggi tempatan dengan syarat wajib lulus bahasa Melayu dan sejarah.

Bahasa Melayu adalah bahasa kebangsaan dan bahasa rasmi mengikut Perkara 152 Perlembagaan. Mana-mana pelajar UEC yang berhasrat memasuki universiti awam di Malaysia wajib memperoleh sekurang-kurangnya gred kepujian (kredit) dalam mata pelajaran bahasa Melayu di peringkat SPM. Ini bagi memastikan mereka mempunyai kompetensi linguistik untuk berinteraksi dan berfungsi dalam ekosistem awam Malaysia.

Selain itu, pengetahuan tentang sejarah tanah air dianggap sebagai asas kepada pembentukan jati diri dan kesetiaan kepada negara. Oleh demikian lulus dalam mata pelajaran sejarah SPM dijadikan syarat wajib yang tidak boleh dikompromi. Ini bagi memastikan setiap mahasiswa di universiti awam, tanpa mengira latar belakang sekolah mereka, dapat berkongsi naratif sejarah watan yang sama.

Pada masa sama aktivis pendidikan yang objektif menggesa Persekutuan Persatuan Lembaga Pengurus Sekolah Cina Malaysia (Dong Zong) menunjukkan keterbukaan bagi membenarkan elemen-elemen sastera, geografi, dan sivik tempatan diintegrasikan ke dalam silibus mereka. Mereka berpandangan pengiktirafan bersifat dua hala; di mana pihak kerajaan juga berhak menuntut penyesuaian terhadap aspirasi nasional dan ia mesti dilaksanakan oleh pihak pengurusan UEC. Harapannya adalah menerusi pendekatan berhati-hati ini, kemasukan pelajar UEC ke universiti awam tidak menggugat Dasar Pendidikan Kebangsaan dan Dasar Kebudayaan Kebangsaan. Bahkan ia boleh bertindak sebagai instrumen integrasi sosial yang menarik mereka graduan Sekolah Persendirian Cina ke dalam arus perdana pembinaan negara.

Seruan Sultan Ibrahim di Dewan Rakyat adalah satu bentuk penegasan cultural authority. Sebagai seorang raja, ia bukanlah kali pertama baginda menekankan pandangan. Pada tahun 2015, baginda mengkritik sistem pendidikan yang menggunakan bahasa Melayu, Mandarin dan Tamil yang dianggapnya menghalang penguasaan bahasa Melayu. Kritikan ini diulang lagi ketika baginda sudah menjadi Agong, di mana baginda menyatakan kehairanan mengapa masih ada rakyat Malaysia tidak boleh berbahasa Melayu, sambil menggesa agar sistem pendidikan negara menjadikan sistem pendidikan sekolah di peringkat rendah hanya satu aliran.

Isu kemampuan menguasai bahasa kebangsaan ini sudah tentu menjadi bahan rangup untuk kumpulan kanan Melayu, di mana penegasan terhadap kebudayaan kebangsaan yang berteraskan bangsa Melayu dipasakkan kembali. Gepena, yang merupakan gabungan kumpulan penulis berbahasa Melayu misalnya pernah mengambil kesempatan dengan meminta aktivis pendidikan Cina tunduk kepada kebudayaan kebangsaan yang berteraskan bangsa dan bahasa Melayu.

Tokoh kanan, dan Timbalan Presiden Muafakat Nasional, Ridhuan Tee Abdullah misalnya mengambil peluang ketidakmampuan graduan sekolah-sekolah Cina persendirian dan keengganan mereka untuk meningkatkan jam pembelajaran bahasa Melayu di sekolah sebagai satu keingkaran, dan mengisyaratkan agar kerajaan menggunakan kuasa dan kekerasan untuk membolehkan bahasa Melayu menjadi keutamaan. Ridhuan juga sering mengkritik papan tanda jalan yang tidak menggunakan bahasa kebangsaan. Dalam satu insiden yang melucukan tetapi dapat menggambarkan bagaimana cultural authority sering dipertengkar dan dipolitikkan, Ridhuan meminta sepanduk Hungry Ghost Festival yang disambut oleh masyarakat Cina ditulis dalam bahasa Melayu.

Selain manipulasi isu bahasa Melayu dalam bidang pendidikan yang ditunggang kumpulan dan tokoh kanan demi menunjukkan kejaguhan masing-masing; bahasa Melayu juga dijadikan bahan politik, untuk tujuan sama. Sebagai contoh, pada tahun 2025, dalam satu skandal sukan yang menyebabkan tujuh pemain antarabangsa digantung Fifa selama 12 bulan kerana memalsukan dokumen berkait status warisan, PAS menggunakan skandal tersebut untuk menjadikan Menteri Dalam Negeri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail sebagai sasaran.

Kerajaan Malaysia mendakwa seramai 23 pemain bola sepak telah diberi taraf kewarganegaraan Malaysia melalui proses naturalisasi sejak tahun 2018, dan ini termasuklah tujuh pemain warisan tersebut. Semua kelulusan ini dibuat mengikut peruntukan undang-undang serta Perlembagaan. Menteri dalam negeri seterusnya berhujah yang setiap permohonan diproses mengikut Perkara 19 Perlembagaan dan Kaedah-kaedah Warganegara yang menetapkan tiga syarat utama iaitu pemohon mesti bermastautin di Malaysia, berkelakuan baik serta mempunyai pengetahuan mencukupi dalam bahasa Melayu. Jawatankuasa Tatatertib Persekutuan Bola Sepak Antarabangsa (Fifa) mengenakan hukuman terhadap Persatuan Bolasepak Malaysia (FAM) dan tujuh pemain ini kerana melanggar Artikel 22 Kod Tatatertib Fifa berkaitan pemalsuan dokumen. Antara pemain terlibat ialah Gabriel Felipe Arrocha, Facundo Tomás Garcés, Rodrigo Julián Holgado, Imanol Javier Machuca, João Vitor Brandão Figueiredo, Jon Irazábal Iraurgui dan Hector Alejandro Hevel Serrano.

Ketua Penerangan PAS Fadhli Shaari dalam usaha memanjangkan skandal ini, dan untuk memerangkap menteri dalam negeri mencabar agar satu video ringkas tujuh pemain naturalisasi berbahasa Melayu disiarkan, memandangkan pengetahuan asas tentang bahasa itu adalah antara syarat wajib memperolehi kewarganegaraan. Sudah tentu Fadhli tidaklah seorang yang naif dan jahil seputar latar belakang skandal ini. Netizen yang bukan ahli Dewan Rakyat malah boleh menghidu kejadian dan angkubah kejadian ini. Fadhli, hanya mahu bermain 'sepak persepsi' untuk menyulitkan hidup seorang menteri; ditakdirkan keadaan terbalik, dan jika Fadhli yang berada di posisi itu, beliau sendiri akan berdepan jerebu solusi yang serupa.

Kedudukan bahasa Melayu sebagai sebahagian jati diri budaya bangsa Melayu dengan itu tidaklah sederhana. Pemuda Umno sebagai contoh menjadikan komitmen untuk terus mempertahankan agama Islam, memartabatkan bangsa Melayu serta memelihara institusi raja Melayu sebagai teras perjuangan. Walaupun komitmen tersebut sebetulnya hanyalah umpan politik dan 'acah-acah Doraemon' sahaja. Dalam banyak keadaan termasuk kes kedudukan bahasa Melayu, kumpulan kanan Melayu dan parti-parti politik misalnya dapat berlindung di sebalik raja Melayu sebagai cultural authority dalam memaksakan agenda politik mereka.

Sudah nasib Oriental Kopi tersedut dalam politik bahasa ini. Mungkin dengan kontroversi dan ancaman boikot ini, rangkaian kopitiam itu akan memperbaiki pemasaran dan persembahannya. Akan tetapi, sementara itu berlaku, ya pilihan raya sudah mendekat, maka politik bahasa sebagai keropok rangup akan terus dikunyah-kunyahi.

fd86b99ff025c2e8: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s call for Malaysia and Egypt to expand educational cooperation beyond Islamic studies is strategically sound.
Indeed, it should be understood as part of a larger effort to strengthen Malaysia’s geopolitical depth in the Middle East and North Africa.
Egypt is not merely a centre of Islamic civilisation.
It is one of the nine pivotal states whose affairs can affect the whole region — not unlike Algeria, Turkey, Indonesia, Pakistan, India, South Africa, Brazil and Mexico.
It is a massive Arab and African power whose geography, diplomatic influence and control of the Suez Canal make it indispensable to international trade and regional security.
President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi’s state visit to Malaysia on Oct 10, 2026, is more than just another diplomatic exchange.
It offers both countries an opportunity to elevate their longstanding relationship into a comprehensive strategic partnership.

Anwar’s emphasis on engineering, medicine, electrical and electronics, artificial intelligence and digital technology reflects an appreciation that modern diplomacy must combine intellectual cooperation with economic and technological capabilities.
Al-Azhar University will remain central to Malaysia’s religious and educational relationship with Egypt.
Its intellectual tradition of moderation, or “wasatiyyah”, continues to provide an important foundation for Islamic scholarship.
Yet bilateral cooperation cannot remain confined to religious education when the geopolitical environment surrounding both countries has become increasingly complicated.
Malaysia needs strategic depth beyond Southeast Asia.

This means cultivating durable relationships with countries capable of providing diplomatic access, economic opportunities, technological collaboration and strategic understanding across several regions.
Egypt offers precisely such an opportunity.
Situated at the intersection of Africa, especially the Horn of Africa, Mediterranean and the Middle East, Egypt occupies a geographical position that few countries can replicate.
Its control of the Suez Canal gives Cairo enormous strategic relevance.
The canal connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, making it one of the world’s most important maritime passages.
For Malaysia, whose economy depends heavily on international trade, disruptions along this corridor can produce serious consequences.
The Red Sea cannot be understood separately from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which connects it to the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean.
Persistent attacks by Yemen’s Houthis against maritime traffic have demonstrated how non-state actors can threaten international shipping, insurance costs and energy security.
Further east, the Strait of Hormuz remains another critical maritime chokepoint through which substantial quantities of global oil and liquefied natural gas move.

Although Egypt does not control either Bab el-Mandeb or Hormuz, its diplomatic networks and proximity to the Red Sea make it an important partner in understanding these interconnected vulnerabilities.
Malaysia must therefore develop a more sophisticated strategic appreciation of the Middle East and North Africa, the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz.
Such understanding cannot be acquired through occasional diplomatic visits alone.
It requires sustained cooperation among universities, maritime institutions, defence establishments, intelligence analysts and diplomatic academies.
Joint research on maritime security, supply-chain resilience, energy transportation and regional conflict management would provide immediate benefits.
Malaysia and Egypt could establish specialised academic programmes examining how instability in West Asia affects Southeast Asian economies.
Their universities could also cooperate in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, medicine, semiconductor technologies and renewable energy.
These initiatives would help transform educational exchanges into instruments of long-term strategic capacity.
The economic foundations are also already strengthening.
Malaysia could use Egypt as a gateway into African and Mediterranean markets, while Egypt could benefit from Malaysia’s established industrial networks and connections throughout Asean.
Both countries should also deepen defence dialogue, particularly in maritime awareness, military education and professional training.
This need not imply a military alliance. Strategic partnerships can strengthen resilience without creating unnecessary security obligations.
Malaysia’s foreign policy has traditionally emphasised non-alignment, constructive engagement and Asean centrality.
Closer cooperation with Egypt would complement rather than contradict these principles.
Indeed, Asean’s strategic interests increasingly extend beyond its immediate geographical boundaries.
Disruptions in the Red Sea or Hormuz can affect Malaysian manufacturers, exporters, consumers and energy markets.
Geographical distance no longer guarantees economic insulation.
The proposed Malaysia-Egypt strategic partnership should consequently be measured not by ceremonial declarations but by tangible institutional achievements.
Joint research centres, student exchanges, investment projects, maritime dialogues and coordinated diplomatic initiatives would demonstrate genuine progress.
Ultimately, Malaysia and Egypt possess complementary strengths.

Egypt offers geographical centrality, diplomatic experience and access to Africa and the Arab world. Malaysia contributes technological capabilities, industrial experience and connectivity to Southeast Asia.

By moving decisively beyond Islamic studies while preserving their historical educational bonds, both countries can construct a partnership capable of navigating an increasingly uncertain international order.
For Malaysia, strategic depth in the Middle East and North Africa is no longer a diplomatic luxury. It is becoming a geopolitical necessity.

02a66f5cbb6850a8: In a previous column, I had argued that the Sedition Act 1948 ought to be struck down unless Parliament amends the Federal Constitution to expressly incorporate it as a permitted restriction on free speech.
As recently as in August, the prime minister himself called for this colonial-era law to be repealed to truly give meaning to Malaysia’s independence.
The fact that the remarks were made at a Merdeka event in UiTM was not lost on me. After all, his Pakatan Harapan coalition has also long championed the cause.
Despite that, to date, no action has been taken by our political leaders to fulfil this pledge.
That has kept the draconian law, which significantly curtails freedom of speech, on the statute books well past its expiry date, and still available for use against ordinary citizens.

Perhaps, our politicians have other priorities presently— or maybe they have no incentive to push the necessary bill to repeal the law. The Dewan Rakyat may be in session, but its present focus is the supply bill to fund the government for 2027.

So what recourse does the rakyat have? The attorney-general (AG), being the guardian of public interest, could move a motion in the Federal Court asking for the Act to be struck down. However, his silence thus far suggests that that item is nowhere on his agenda.
Will the Bar Council, an NGO, activists or a member of the public pick the matter up? No one knows.
Yet, as I have consistently maintained, the courts possess ample constitutional authority to move the dial given the inertia shown by our elected representatives.

In my view the jurisprudence related to oath of office and constitutional judicial power read with Article 4 is ripe enough for the legal community to bring forth strategic constitutional challenges before the relevant courts, including by inviting the court to exercise its suo motu powers.

The oath of office, which binds judges to “preserve, protect and defend” the constitutional rights of all Malaysians, imposes upon the courts a sacred duty not merely to safeguard those rights, but to actively facilitate their empowerment.

In my view, the process should involve very little red tape. Following the practice in India, a letter to the High Court or the Federal Court should be sufficient to set the wheels of justice in motion—since the judicial power invoked is exercised directly according to the oath of office and not under Article 121(1).

However, the courts should not act on its own. It should invite the AG, the Malaysian Bar, the Advocates Association of Sarawak, and the Sabah Law Society to weigh in on whether the Sedition Act can truly coexist within the constitutional supremacy regime.
No one can accuse the courts of going rogue, especially since our political leaders have already expressed publicly an intention to do the very same thing.
So, will the legal industry make an attempt?

cef6d0807cbc1074: The Budget 2027 allocation for the health ministry (MOH) and public healthcare has been raised to RM47.7bil, only RM1.2 billion extra which is the smallest increase in five years.
This falls well short of the Pakatan Harapan election promise to target 5% of GDP for public sector health expenditure in terms of both money and percentage.
At 10.3% of the total federal budget and 2.1% of GDP, the budget for the MOH has hardly changed in the last five years.

This shows that it is still “business as usual” in terms of public sector health expenditure and the small increase in the ministry’s budget barely exceeds the general inflation rate let alone medical inflation.

The government has met its longstanding promise to solve the issue of contract doctors and must be given credit for that. Anwar claims that MOH will create more than 9,000 vacancies to absorb the current contract doctors and newly trained housemen.
The allocation for the number of positions shows this, and the promise that new batches of trained housemen will be appointed directly to permanent positions is likely to be kept.

This demonstrates that coordination with the public service department (JPA) and the political will to solve the position problem through planning can be effective. It has taken more than a decade, but better late than never.
The new medical officers looking to serve in the public sector are still looking for higher pay, flexibility in appointments and job security.

The increase to the incentives for nurses and paramedics is only RM100 per month and does little to address concerns about low pay compared to peers in the private sector and overseas, such as in Singapore and the Middle East.
Brain drain is considered severe; this budget policy announcement is only a small, welcome adjustment and does not address the systemic issue of staff retention.
The realisation that more ambulances are needed for effective emergency care and the decision to purchase additional ambulances is a welcome change in management.
Nonetheless, there still are too many gaps in the public healthcare system.
With this small budget increase and without complementary policies and the necessary political will, these issues will not be resolved.
Some of these issues are not about money at all. They are about management and changing old-style human resource processes.

On the other hand, spending for public-private healthcare has increased from RM144 million to RM200 million for next year. This is a substantial increase for the outsourcing of public sector patients to the private sector.

An earlier government report stated that RM66.5 million was spent on 24,000 outsourced patients. If the government can maintain this rate, it could free up more than 70,000 public sector patients next year.
While this would improve waiting times in public hospitals, it would probably have only a minimal impact compared to the estimated 19 million outpatient visits in 2024.
However, for certain medical treatments and procedures, this could have a meaningful impact on waiting times.
With the Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme now covering 14 specialty areas, the increase in allocation will be welcome news for public sector patients but it is a form of privatisation.

The policy announcement regarding MediAsas and price transparency in private healthcare is also a form of privatisation and likely to have a greater impact on access to care and help to keep medical inflation in check.
While these might not require significant budget allocation from the government, the government will certainly need to step up its regulatory efforts.
This is the real challenge. If healthcare is to be balanced between public and private providers, then regulation and management must improve.

54f95897dfd35ce6: Dalam artikel ini saya ingin mengulas tulisan sahabat saya A Kathirasen berjudul Poets, Philosophers and Policy: The moral language of Budget 2027, yang mengupas bahasa falsafah, puisi dan agama dalam belanjawan Anwar Ibrahim. Mesej artikel tersebut adalah bacaan penulis sendiri betapa Anwar cuba memberi suatu mesej ‘kemanusiaan sejagat’ dalam terjemahan fiskal dan angka-angka wang ringgit dalam alokasi-alokasi masing-masing.

Kathirasen ingin menarik perhatian kepada asas bahawa belanjawan adalah aspek kematangan kemanusiaan, bukan semata-mata wang kocek di sini dan sana untuk dihabiskan. Penulis veteran itu juga ingin mengkiaskan usaha Anwar untuk mensejagatkan isu keperluan daripada pengasingan perkauman. Dalam artikel ini saya akan memanjangkan tafsiran Kathirasen dengan membawa mesej saya sendiri, iaitu, bahasa dan rujukan yang digunakan membawa konsep pemerintahan dan penjagaan negara memerlukan suatu bahasa Melayu-global.

Ada dua aspek yang ingin saya sentuh tentang penggunaan rujukan pelbagai kaum dan agama serta pelbagai sumber ketamadunan manusia dari kitab suci agama, kepada falsafah pemikir dan puisi pujangga. Pertama adalah tuduhan ‘liberal’ kepada sesiapa Melayu Muslim yang menggunakan sumber pemikiran atau falsafah dan refleksi spiritual daripada selain sumber Islam.
Keduanya adalah apakah yang saya maksudkan sebagai bahasa lingua franca Melayu global sebagai hamparan kepada pemikiran Anwar sebagai intelek Melayu-Islam.

Yang pertama adalah tuduhan yang selalu diajukan kepada sesiapa yang membawa argumen atau perbahasan atau konsep daripada pemikiran, refleksi dan falsafah dari selain Islam Sunni akan membawa tuduhan ‘liberal’ dan merosakkan serta menyesatkan orang Islam. Sebagai seorang ilmuan seni bina, saya amat memahami keperluan menggunakan sumber-sumber konsep, pemikiran dan prinsip-prinsip seni bina dari Barat seperti pemikiran Frank Lloyd Wright, Louis Sullivan, William Morris, Walter Gropius, Mies van der Rohe dan Le Corbusier. Sumber-sumber falsafah dan pemikiran dari Amerika Syarikat, England, Perancis dan Jerman amat perlu saya garapkan dalam memikir semula teori atau prinsip seni bina Islam, seni bina Malaysia dan seni bina Melayu moden.

Peminjaman pemikiran dari sumber luar atau lain dari kaum dan agama kita sendiri bukan bermaksud mengagungkan atau mengkiblatkan Barat atau Timur tetapi memberi pengiktirafan bahawa bangsa-bangsa manusia yang lain melalui pemodenan dan kesedaran dalam tahap yang berbeza serta waktu yang lebih awal dari kita di Malaysia. Arus revolusi industri meranapkan hubungan masyarakat dan pemerintah serta pemikiran ‘enlightenment’ pula mencabar tafsiran kehidupan, kosmos dan geografi duni daripada hanya interpretasi gereja sahaja.

Negara kita di rantau ini, walaupun mempunyai segala macam telefon pintar, AI, serta teknologi baharu yang terkini masih melalui suatu pertembungan antara pemikiran sains, politik dan agama yang telah dilalui orang di Barat dunia lebih 200 tahun sebelumnya.

Kita Melayu sampai lewat sikit. Maka itu penggunaan serta peminjaman konsep, istilah dan pemikiran daripada selain Islam menggambarkan keupayaan seorang Melayu menggarap dan membentuk suatu belanjawan yang bernyawakan moral, wawasan jauh dan ketamadunan kemanusiaan.

Belanjawan negara adalah bukan semata-mata belanjawan korporat yang tahu untung rugi sahaja. Maka itu adalah tidak wajar pada sesiapa yang akan menuding jari “nah itu bunyi orang Melayu-Islam liberal” ataupun “nah itu bunyi orang yang dijajah pemikiran kolonial dari Barat dan dari sumber musuh Islam”.

Sebagai ilmuan, semua para cerdik pandai tahu bahawa kebenaran merentasi kaum dan agama kerana kaum dan agama yang difahami itu telah disempitkan oleh golongan yang disuruh menjaga integriti warisan tersebut. Namun demikian, penjaga warisan ugama yang berpendidikan tidak pelbagai disiplin dan ilmu hanya dapat melihatnya dengan satu belah teropong sahaja.

Perkara kedua adalah bagaimana Anwar memainkan peranan seorang Melayu global dan bukan Melayu-parti atau Melayu-ustaz. Untuk menjadi suatu bangsa yang berjaya, orang Melayu perlu mengetahui pelbagai sumber pemikiran yang datang dari pelbagai bangsa dan budaya. Seperti juga Hang Tuah yang telah memohon ayahandanya untuk beliau mempelajari lebih daripada 10 bahasa asing. Melayu yang mempunyai akses kepada pemikiran daripadapelbagai sumber lain tidak akan terbantut kepada retorik perpaduan Melayu untuk kuasa serta kesucuan agama tanpa kematangan global dan menyeluruh. Saya sering mengajar pelajar PhD bahawa semua ilmu adalah tafsiran orang yang hendak menggunakannya pada ketika itu dan dalam konteks kefahaman teknologi, sains dan budaya manusia selainnya sahaja. Maka, sesuatu ilmu seperti ilmu agama boleh diperluaskan atau diperkecilkan mengikut kehendak seseorang. Ilmu perlu melimpah kepada pemikiran dan tafsiran setiap masa berubah dan juga perubahan untuk berpindah kerana situasi semasa.

Akhir sekali, saya mencadangkan janganlah kita terlalu pantas menghukum ‘sesat’ atau ‘liberal’ kepada sesiapa hanya kerana mereka menggunakan istilah luar yang kita sendiri tidak tahu hujung pangkal. Perkara pokok yang perlu dijiwai daripada artikel saya dan Kathirasen adalah belanjawan bukan semata-mata angka yang diagih-agihkan kepada semua kememterian. Seperkara lagi adalah penggunaan istilah, konsep dan falsafah yang merentasi jurang kaum, agama dan budaya adalah keupayaan berfikir luar daripada kepompong tradisi. Hanya dengan percampuran dan menjunamkan diri ke dalam budaya lain maka barulah kita boleh menggarap solusi baharu serta arah tuju sama yang cekal dan kental.

fc7c7d8e2be54e0a: Cisco “strongly” implored customers to patch yet another critical, make-me-root vulnerability in its Secure Email Gateway (SEG), one that has already been exploited in zero-day attacks. A Cisco spokesperson told The Register that the critical vuln, which received a 9.8 out of 10 CVSS rating, affects “a limited number of customers.” The bug, now tracked as CVE‑2026‑76519, allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to write files and execute commands with root privileges on the appliance’s operating system - simply by sending a malicious email. In separate Wednesday advisories, both the networking vendor and the US government warned that attackers were exploiting the latest SEG vulnerability before Cisco issued a fix. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and set a Saturday deadline for federal agencies to fix the issue. “We are aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability,” the spokesperson said, but declined to answer our questions about how many appliances had been compromised, and what attackers were doing with this access after exploiting the bug. “We strongly urge customers to upgrade to a fixed software release and follow additional recommendations and hardening guidance in our advisory,” the spokesperson said. The flaw exists in SEG’s Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature, and it’s due to improper handling of email attachments. An attacker could exploit the bug by sending an email with a malicious attachment, and a successful exploit would allow them to write files and execute commands as root on the compromised appliance. This vulnerability affects both physical and virtual SEG appliances running a vulnerable release of Cisco AsyncOS Software if both of the following conditions are met: The File Reputation service, which is part of Cisco AMP, is enabled and assigned to a mail policy. The Content Scanner Tools version is earlier than 25.3.0.5525. Cisco's Wednesday advisory includes steps organizations can take to determine whether File Reputation is enabled and which Content Scanner Tools version is installed - so give that a read if you are unsure. Upgrading to a fixed Cisco AsyncOS Software release will patch the security hole, and there are no workarounds. The vendor recommends any customers who are running Cisco AsyncOS Software releases earlier than v 16.5 migrate to 16.5.0-780. In its alert, Cisco said it became aware of active exploitation in October. This is the second such zero-day in SEG in as many months. In mid-September, Cisco warned customers that criminals were exploiting a similar bug in SEG, tracked as CVE-2026-76461, that also turns a malicious email into root access. In January, attackers exploited another critical AsyncOS flaw, CVE-2025-20393, to break into Cisco SEG appliances and install persistence mechanisms. That bug eventually scored a perfect 10.®
9eb295a80fa64f4f: Earlier this week, a mass hack of refrigeration systems at an estimated 700 supermarkets throughout France caused them to suddenly malfunction, causing spoilage of untold tons of perishables and, in some cases, fires. As is now the norm, basic cybersecurity would have prevented it.

French authorities say the systems, made up of entire fleets of refrigerators and freezers throughout a store, were hacked. More specifically, Internet-connected controllers that allow technicians to remotely administer the store-wide systems were compromised. The unknown attackers responsible then activated defrosters long enough for the fridges to reach temperatures as high as 50° Celsius (122° Fahrenheit). By the time the mass compromise was discovered, food was spoiled, and in some cases their electrical systems caught fire.
The hacks that didn't have to happen

Multiple security advisories and public research reports show that all three of the controller models reportedly hacked in the incident—sold by Danfoss of Denmark and Dixell and its parent company Copeland in the US—contained critical vulnerabilities that allow attackers to remotely log in to the devices with the same system rights as administrators. Until recently, Danfoss controllers, for instance, used a credential that changes each day. The password is generated by the publicly available firmware based on the date. A hacker who takes the time to analyze the code can do the same thing on any device that hasn’t received a recent update. Daily passwords are identical across models located in hundreds or thousands of stores.

8df95ca30f9db531: A YouTuber who’s gained a following for trolling AI interview bots brought his own computing companion to an interview with him. As chaos ensued, viewers learned that having an AI as your interview agent isn't a good idea. Graham Dot Zip is a comedian whose YouTube channel has blown up recently thanks to videos of him demonstrating the absurdity of AI bots used to conduct early-stage interviews with job candidates. AI interviewers have become quite the phenomenon in recent months, and not one that job seekers are fond of, with plenty of videos and social media posts documenting hate for them. Enter Graham and his trolling of various interview bots. Some videos have garnered nearly 2 million views in the past few weeks. In one, he answers every question with gibberish responses that the AI parrots as if they’re cogent responses. In another, he has the bot gushing unnecessary pleasantries and thanks as the two go back and forth trying to be professionally polite. While it’s amusing to watch an AI try to deal with interviewees who are obviously trolling them, Graham’s most recent video is what really merits a mention here. In this instance, Graham pits his own AI representative, which he created to handle the interview for him, against an AI interviewer presented as acting on behalf of a company. Victor, Graham’s “representative,” misstates Graham’s qualifications and misrepresents his participation in a particular project. Then comes the kicker: When asked about salary expectations, Victor claims Graham would be happy to take the job for around $60,000 a year, which Graham vehemently disagrees with, saying he was looking at somewhere between $140K and $150K. The AI recruiter refuses to go above $90K. Graham steps out for a moment, and the two bots decide to schedule a follow-up interview without him. Upon his return, both are stuck in a loop thanking each other for their time and saying goodbye, seemingly without the ability to terminate the call. While funny, there’s a bit of a dystopian nightmare to be found here, too. Although Graham may be trolling the AI interviewer, he's still been essentially cornered by his own AI bot’s poor ability to negotiate and refusal to listen to his instructions not to lie about his qualifications and his desired salary range. It’s a worrying prospect in the era of agentic commerce, where AI companies are trying to create AI agents that can shop for us and undertake other commercial exchanges. Who’s to say those bots are any better at negotiating for a good deal than Victor? If there’s anything to be learned from a growing number of videos of people trolling AI interview bots, convincing them they’re dying, and burning through those valuable AI tokens, it’s that, yet again, there are things AI is good for and things it’s not. Putting on a human mask and talking to human job candidates, frankly, isn’t something they ought to be doing - job seekers don’t think so, at least, despite AI HR departments seemingly becoming the norm. Given Victor’s poor negotiation skills, they probably shouldn’t be engaged in anything to do with trying to get consumers a deal, either. As the AI hellscape grows around us, with seemingly no limit to what a bot-pushing firm will try to sell, all we can do is laugh, it seems. Luckily, there are plenty of dumb bots out there ready to make AI providers and the companies using their services the butt of many an internet joke. ®

29ad242422527ec3: Despite previous controversies, it seems like the lords of Linux are warming to AI-assisted coding. The penguin's kernel community has agreed to stop asking coders to disclose whether they used bots to help with their contributions. And Linux kernel supremo Linus Torvalds has made clear that he opposes "stupid" AI disclosure rules as long as people understand the code they're submitting. "The Maintainers Summit reached consensus to deprecate the Assisted-by Tag," said Sasha Levin, a Linux kernel developer and engineer at Nvidia, in a message to the Linux kernel mailing list last week. "Remove the documentation requiring it." The policy had said that those using "any sort of advanced coding tool in the creation of [their] patch" should acknowledge that through the addition of an "Assisted-by" tag in the commit message. The AI labeling proposal initially took shape in July 2025. It became part of the documentation in January 2026. This was shortly after Torvalds said that he was fairly positive about vibe coding as a way for people to get into programming, but remained skeptical about its effect on software maintainability. Since then, he's warmed to AI tool usage. AI attribution wasn't an issue when the generated code was obvious, buggy, and bad. But in the past year or so, AI coding agents started producing code that is of acceptable quality for the purposes of the Linux kernel community. "LLMs are good enough now," said Greg Kroah-Hartman, a veteran Linux kernel maintainer, at the Linux Foundation's Open Source Summit in South Korea in August. "They've gotten good enough to find bugs because LLMs, AI, are just pattern matchers and code is nothing but patterns in a specific format." Cautious acceptance hasn't erased concerns about errors slipping through unnoticed, accountability, and coding agents reproducing copyrighted code. There's also still a stigma in some circles around the use of AI tools. Those who have spent years honing software skills, coding with limited assistance from tools, may disparage developers who don't understand the code they conjure with a prompt. Rapid change will do that – in the space of a few years, software production practices have changed drastically, and software quality, security, and maintenance practices have yet to fully adjust. The leading makers of AI coding agents – Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, and the like – are doing their best to promote AI-driven projects as better than anything a human developer could manage. Yet even they differ in their AI attribution practices. Claude adds provenance messages by default, but Codex does not. In fields such as advertising and art, content provenance can help assess misinformation and human creative input. For code, the focus tends to be more on functionality than form. In a prior discussion of the merits of the tag requirement, Jeff Layton, a Linux kernel developer with Red Hat, explained the rationale for reversing course. First, he said, not everyone abides by the policy. Second, he said, "it basically serves as free advertising for proprietary LLM companies." And third, he said, "it's not clear why we want to collect this info in the first place." Some kernel contributors still see value in the tagging requirement. "I'm not happy removing the tag without adding another mechanism for required disclosure," said Laurent Pinchart, a Linux kernel dev and founder of Ideas on Board, in a mailing list post on Tuesday. "Without that, I can foresee submitters pushing back on the question." Pinchart challenged the argument that AI labeling rules will just be ignored. "What this is about is setting our expectations, telling what we want and what we don't want," said Pinchart. "There's still value in that, and I'd argue there's even more value now. There will be people who won't care, there will be people who cheat. We've always had those, we'll keep having them, and we'll keep rejecting their contributions. I really don't get the unenforceable argument here." Linus Torvalds responded with an emphatic rejection of tool usage declarations. He wrote: What you are about is something entirely different. It has nothing to do with "expectations", and it has everything to do with your hangups. I don't understand this whole idiotic concept of "don't use AI for X". Here's a new rule just for you: don't use compilers for any of your kernel submissions. Because if you can't show that you really understand what the machine is actually doing by writing your code in assembler, then I don't want to see your code contribution. You clearly aren't competent if you can't write it that way. And btw, you had better not use an editor to write that commit message either. Because I need you to show me that you can actually write a good commit message without using tools that make it easy to backspace and hide the mistakes you made while typing. Ok? Because otherwise those tool-assisted commits of yours clearly aren't showing that you know what you are doing. Do you not see how UTTERLY STUPID those kinds of rules would be? So no. We're not going to make stupid rules that say "you can't use tools for X". The kind of expectations *I* have is that people do their best and I expect people to understand what they are doing. But that understanding has very little to do with what tools they use. And quite honestly, in my experience, the people I respect and call intelligent are not the ones that shy away from using new and interesting tools. ®

15182b3efcde6535: Researchers at security startup Xbow used OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model to help chain three zero-day vulnerabilities in Chrome into an exploit capable of executing code outside the browser's sandbox on Windows machines. Xbow estimates that this could affect about one billion users worldwide. Google fixed all three, and paid the Xbow team a $250,000 bounty, its top reward for a Chrome full-chain exploit. The payout also proves a nice return on investment for the human bug hunters - Brendan Dolan-Gavitt, Andres Luksenberg, Baul Lee, and Willem Pinckaers - who spent just six days during the Black Hat and DEF CON conferences and about $40,000 in token charges to discover the vulnerabilities and build the attack chain. “The number on the check is impressive, but the time it took our team, with the help of a publicly available AI model, to break in is even more impressive,” Xbow CEO and founder Oege de Moor said on Tuesday. “A three letter intelligence-agency veteran told me that his team used to spend six months trying to identify this kind of vulnerability and get total access. We did it in six days.” In a separate technical writeup about the attack chain, Dolan-Gavitt detailed the work done by humans and AI agents. Agents, using OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol model, searched source code, tested the team’s hypotheses, and developed proofs of concept and exploit stages, he said. Meanwhile, the AI pen-testing security startup’s researchers chose targets, provided context, challenged the agents’ results, and decided which attack components to chain. "We did apply a fair bit of our own human expertise and judgment," he wrote. Crossing two security boundaries in 3 steps Google’s Chrome browser uses several layers of security to protect users, and this includes sandboxes - barriers to contain compromised code and ensure that someone who hacks an individual website can’t take over the entire computer. This includes deploying the V8 sandbox to prevent any memory corruption flaws in the V8 JavaScript engine from impacting other memory. The V8 sandbox sits inside the operating-system process sandbox, and this nested design means that escaping V8's memory restrictions doesn't automatically grant native code execution. Even if an attacker achieves native code execution inside Chrome's renderer, the outer process sandbox restricts access to the rest of the machine. “The chain crossed both boundaries in three vulnerability stages,” abusing Chrome to run code on Windows machines, Dolan-Gavitt wrote. The attack combines a V8 compiler bug, an animated-WebP decoder bug, and a memory-safety bug in Crashpad. The first vulnerability is in Maglev, V8's mid-tier optimizing compiler, and it’s due to a reused, mutable boxed number during deoptimization. This gives attackers read and write access throughout V8's pointer-compression cage. The second stage, the animated-WebP bug, is a V8 sandbox escape. “But rather than attacking the sandbox itself we exploited a property that the V8 sandbox deliberately does not enforce and that Blink incorrectly assumed it could trust,” Dolan-Gavitt explained. “Finally, the exploit used an overflow in Crashpad to cross the final outer process boundary and achieve unsandboxed code execution on the host.” While Google patched all three security issues, and Chrome installs updates on its own, a fix only takes effect once the user relaunches the browser. If you use Chrome, make sure you are running version 152.0.7977.82 or later. The time and money spent to achieve a full chain Chrome exploit illustrate - yet again - that “the bar is significantly lower” for attackers armed with LLMs, Dolan-Gavitt wrote. “Defend accordingly.”®

"We are aware of exploitation in the wild affecting a limited number of customers at the time of disclosure," the vendor said in its advisory.
